title: CI: drop graphviz check from lane pre-commit toolchain verify
body:
pre-commit's Verify step checked for graphviz, but `dot` belongs to the st-sim dep_gen smoke (deps_viewer), not pre-commit — the check aborted the job on a runner without graphviz even though pre-commit does not need it.

Also documents the cpu-runner provisioning contract in the lane header: every cpu agent needs the same dnf toolchain (cmake ninja-build gcc-c++ clang-tools-extra graphviz gtest-devel python3-devel) and a clean python site — no simpler/simpler_setup/_task_interface in system or user site-packages, the same contract ci.yml's NPU jobs rely on (a stale install satisfies pip under --system-site-packages and shadows the fresh venv install).

title: CI: revert lane packaging venv to plain (ci.yml parity)
body: #1626 switched the lane's packaging venv to `--system-site-packages`, but ci.yml's packaging venv is plain. On runners whose system site carries nanobind (e.g. conda-based cpu-4), the system-site venv treats nanobind as satisfied and never installs it, so `verify_packaging.sh`'s wheel build fails at `find_package(nanobind)`. Plain venv installs nanobind into the venv and matches ci.yml.

title: CI: report /run-cpu lane results back on the PR
body:
The /run-cpu lane run is standalone (issue_comment runs attach no checks to the PR), so results were only visible inside the run. This adds a watcher that posts them back:

- `ci-self-cpu-button.yml`: `run-name: /run-cpu PR ${{ github.event.issue.number }}` — the run's display title now carries the PR number.
- `ci-self-cpu-report.yml` (new): `workflow_run` on the button workflow; parses the PR number from the display title, lists the lane jobs, and comments `✅/❌ + per-job status + run link` on the PR. Runs on `[self-hosted, cpu]` so it is not delayed by the congestion the lane exists for.

Only comments when the admin gate passed (lane jobs exist); denied or skipped button runs stay silent.

title: CI: lane T1 jobs use setup-python 3.10 with pip cache (ci.yml parity)
body: The cpu runner's system python is 3.9, but the repo uses `zip(strict=)` (3.10+) in worker.py — the lane's T1 venvs failed 46 ut tests with `TypeError: zip() takes no keyword arguments`.\n\nT1 jobs now mirror ci.yml's GitHub-hosted pattern: `actions/setup-python@v6` 3.10 + `actions/cache` for `~/.cache/pip` + plain `pip install` (no venv). The toolchain python is isolated, so runner system/user python state (version, site-packages pollution) can no longer affect T1; the runner contract shrinks to the dnf binaries. packaging keeps a venv (`verify_packaging.sh` requires an activated one) but creates it from the setup-python 3.10. T3 (NPU) jobs unchanged.

title: CI: lane T1 venvs use the runner python3 with a pip cache
body: The cpu runner's HCE image ships python3.9 (no python3.10 package in its repos; `actions/setup-python` has no prebuilt toolchain for HuaweiCloudEulerOS). The repo declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, so T1 jobs create plain venvs from the runner's `python3` and keep the pip cache — first run downloads once, later runs hit the cache; the venv isolates T1 from system/user python state. T3 (NPU) unchanged. No runner-side python install needed.\n\nDepends on #1631 (the runner's 3.9 caught `zip(strict=)` — a 3.10-only keyword the repo's 3.10 CI never exercised).

title: Fix: zip(strict=) breaks Python 3.9 support
body: worker.py used `zip(..., strict=True)` (3.10+ keyword) while `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python = ">=3.9"`. Replaced with an explicit length check + plain zip, preserving strict semantics on both 3.9 and 3.10. The CI ut job runs setup-python 3.10, so this never surfaced; the cpu lane's runner python (3.9) caught it (46 ut failures: `TypeError: zip() takes no keyword arguments`).

title: CI: restore pip upgrade in lane T1 venv steps
body: The setup-python rewrite dropped `pip install --upgrade pip`, leaving T1 venvs on the runner's pip 21.3.1 (python3.9 ensurepip). Round 7 hit a sympy hash mismatch during `pip install torch` — a corrupted pip-cache entry from an interrupted earlier run that old pip reused. Upgrading pip first restores sane cache/hash handling.\n\nAlso deleted the stale `Linux-pip-*` actions-cache entries and the runner's `~/.cache/pip` should be cleared (`rm -rf ~/.cache/pip`) so the next run downloads fresh and re-uploads clean.

title: CI: lane pre-commit diff against canonical main and PR head
body: Round 8: pre-commit failed with `CalledProcessError: git diff 2a85eb93..259f2336`. `--to-ref` used `github.sha` (default-branch latest) while `--from-ref` came from `origin/main` — for a fork PR the checkout is the fork, whose main lags and which lacks the new canonical commits, so the diff range doesn't exist locally.\n\nFix: fetch the canonical repo's main (`git fetch https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git main` — the runner's github extraheader authenticates it) and diff `merge-base(FETCH_HEAD, HEAD)..inputs.ref` — both endpoints exist in the checkout.

title: Fix: make session-timeout test race-free under runner load
body: The driver armed the session timeout at a fixed 3 s, racing the child's pytest startup: on a loaded shared runner (the cpu lane runs 5 T1 jobs in parallel on one box) startup can exceed 3 s, so the timeout dumps the child before it forks and `_grandchild_deadlock_sentinel` never appears. Tuning the constant (30 s, 300 s) only widens the race window and slows the test.\n\nInstead the dump is now **event-driven**: the grandchild writes a ready marker the moment it reaches the sentinel, and a driver watcher thread fires the real conftest handler (`os.kill(self, SIGALRM)`) when the marker appears. The session timeout is demoted to a 60 s fail-safe bound (same as the driver's existing subprocess timeout). The test stays fast (startup + epsilon) and cannot race the startup at any load; a real regression still fails at the 60 s bound with the sentinel missing from the dump.

title: Fix: gate packaging and the profiling smoke off tests-only changes
body:
## Summary

`packaging-matrix` ran on any diff that touched `tests/` — a change confined to `tests/ut/py/` (e.g. #1634) booked two packaging jobs that build, install, and smoke the same wheel it did not touch. The rules justified this with two claims; **both were false**:

1. **"`tests/` is in the sdist `include`"** — no sdist configuration exists in `pyproject.toml`. The entire packaging surface is `wheel.packages = ["simpler_setup", "python/simpler"]`; `tests/` is not in the wheel at all.
2. **"`verify_packaging.sh` runs a `tests/st/` file as its entry-point smoke"** — true, but it is one **fixed** file (`paged_attention_unroll/test_paged_attention_unroll.py --help`, run from the source tree, not from the wheel). A changed payload file is exercised by the scene-test job that reads the same corpus.

This completes the symmetry #1607 left half-finished: it removed `examples/` from both product jobs' reach (profiling's payload lives there), but `tests/` stayed in with a reason that did not survive contact with the workflow.

## The change

```yaml
TESTS_ONLY='^(tests/)'           # same shape as EXAMPLES_ONLY='^examples/'
packaging-matrix:      !non_code_only && !examples_only && !tests_only
profiling-flags-smoke: (a2a3_changed || a5_changed) && !examples_only && !tests_only
```

New axis is fail-open like every other (unrecognized paths flip it on), and the empty-diff guard sets `tests_only=false` alongside the other corpus flag. Rules + `docs/ci.md` updated with the correction; the stale sdist claim is deleted from both.

## Testing

- [x] Replayed the exact grep chain from the workflow against representative file sets (§7 of the rule — behavior first, before changing anything):
  - `tests/ut/...`, `tests/st/...`, mixed, and the payload file itself → **both jobs skip** (UT/ST jobs still run as before)
  - `pyproject.toml`, `simpler_setup/`, `src/`, root `conftest.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` → **both run**
  - docs-only / `.gitignore`-only → both skip
- [x] YAML parses; all seven `detect-changes` outputs consumed
- [x] This PR changes `ci.yml`, which is deliberately outside `NON_CODE` — the full matrix is expected and correct

title: Fix: event-driven drain in session-timeout HUNG handler
body:
The handler slept a fixed 2 s after SIGUSR1 before printing the HUNG group and SIGTERMing the children. On a loaded runner (the cpu lane runs 5 jobs in parallel on one box) a starved descendant can take longer than 2 s to run its faulthandler dump — the dump then dies with the SIGTERM and the HUNG body lacks the frames that caused the hang (`_grandchild_deadlock_sentinel` missing).

Drain until the pump's output stops growing (bounded at 10 s, quiet-detected at ~1 s of no new output), so slow signal delivery still lands in the group; children are SIGTERMed only once the output has settled.

Rationale: this is the same fixed-budget-vs-slow-process pattern as the session-timeout test's 3 s — event-driven instead of constant-tuning. Locally the race-free test passes in every configuration (3.9/3.10, full suite, under multi-process load ×20); this change hardens the production handler against the one unreproducible-locally case (real 5-job load on the runner).

title: Docs: give the local onboard sweep the same marker shape as CI
body:

**Also fixed, the deferred `ci.yml` comments** — the two that claimed the SDMA step runs "on its own dedicated device(s)", flagged in #1617 and left until ci.yml was next touched for a substantive reason. Device disjointness holds only on aarch64 (`task-submit --device auto`); the x86_64 branch shares `${DEVICE_RANGE}` and ordering is the separation. This change touches `ci.yml`, so the full matrix runs — which was the reason it had been deferred.

## Testing

title: Fix: serialize faulthandler dumps in session-timeout handler
body: The handler SIGUSR1'd the dispatched pytest and every descendant at once; their faulthandler dumps then wrote to the same pipe concurrently and **interleaved at the byte level**, splitting frame names across lines. The session-timeout test failed intermittently with `_grandchild_deadlock_sentinel` missing from the HUNG body — even though the dump contained it (verified on the cpu runner: the sentinel string is split into fragments, only `sentinel` survives contiguously).\n\nFix: signal one process at a time and drain until the output settles (~1 s of quiet, bounded at 10 s) before signaling the next, so each dump lands intact. The drain helper is shared with the pre-SIGTERM settle. This also makes the production HUNG dumps readable under load.

title: [Code Health] Deduplicate jobs between ci.yml and ci-self-cpu.yml workflows
body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Other (please specify in description) — `.github/workflows/` CI workflows

### Description

`ci-self-cpu.yml` (the emergency CPU lane) duplicates large parts of `ci.yml`:

1. **`detect-changes` job** — the NON_CODE vocabulary + all gating axes are copied verbatim between the two workflows. This has already drifted **twice**: `examples_only` never reached the lane (#1607) and `tests_only` did not either (#1635). `.claude/rules/ci-change-detection.md` now mandates "any change to an axis means two files, same commit" plus a two-file outputs-consistency grep — a permanent sync tax on every gate change.
2. **T1 no-hardware jobs** (pre-commit, ut, packaging, profiling-flags-smoke, st-sim-a2a3/a5) and **T3 NPU jobs** (ut-a2a3, st-onboard-a2a3, ut-a5, st-onboard-a5) exist in both workflows, differing only in runner selection and setup (ci.yml: `setup-python` + no venv; lane: plain venv + pip cache; both wrap NPU tests in `task-submit`).
3. **Per-job scaffolding** — checkout-with-`repository`/`ref`, `Cache pip packages`, and venv creation steps are repeated across the lane's 10+ jobs.

Every change to a gate axis or a job's steps must be made twice; the drift history is already two incidents. The lane's own header comment and the rules file both carry "keep the two in sync" notes.

### Location

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ci-self-cpu.yml`
- `.claude/rules/ci-change-detection.md` (documents the sync requirement)

### Proposed Fix

- **Highest value: extract `detect-changes` into one canonical implementation** (a reusable workflow via `workflow_call` or a composite action) consumed by both `ci.yml` and `ci-self-cpu.yml`, eliminating the two-copy drift. The rule's outputs-consistency grep then checks one file.
- **Parameterize the job bodies**: a reusable workflow whose caller passes the differences as inputs — `runs-on` targets, setup variant (setup-python path vs plain-venv + pip cache), arch selection. T1/T3 job definitions exist once.
- **Extract the repeated step blocks** (checkout-with-ref, pip cache, venv) into composite actions.
- Constraint: the lane must stay triggerable via `workflow_call` from the `/run-cpu` button under the fork-PR read-only token, and via `workflow_dispatch` for manual runs — reusable workflows are compatible with both.

### Priority

Medium (no impact today, but the duplication has already caused two gating drifts)

title: [Code Health] Device-phase/strace timing buffer is copied device↔host on every simpler_run, unconditionally and unaffected by its own enable gates
body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

Every `simpler_run` (i.e. every round / every token on the decode hot path) performs **three device↔host transfers** around the AICPU device-phase / strace timing buffer, and **all three run unconditionally**, even though the only consumer of that data is gated off by two separate switches.

Per-run transfers:

| # | Operation | Direction | Payload |
| - | --------- | --------- | ------- |
| 1 | `ensure_device_wall_buffer()` H2D reset | Host→Device | whole buffer reset to sentinel |
| 2 | `read_device_wall_ns()` first `rtMemcpy` | Device→Host | AICPU phase region (`kThreads × NUM_AICPU_PHASES`) |
| 3 | `read_device_wall_ns()` second `rtMemcpy` | Device→Host | task-timing tail (`kThreads × NUM_TASK_TIMING_SLOTS`) |

Payload sizes (16 B/record):

- **a2a3** (`kThreads = 6`): phase region 960 B, tail 1536 B; H2D reset 2496 B.
- **a5** (`kThreads = 14`): phase region 2240 B, tail 3584 B; H2D reset 5824 B.

Two observations about how this data is used vs. how it is transferred:

1. **The transfers are not gated, but the consumer is.** The only reader of `last_device_wall_ns()` / `last_device_phase_ns()` / `last_task_slot_*()` is `emit_device_phase_markers()`, which is double-gated: compile-time `SIMPLER_HOST_STRACE` (so `STRACE_DEV_SPAN_AT` compiles to nothing when off) and runtime `device_profiling_enabled()` (env `SIMPLER_DEVICE_STRACE_ENABLE != 0`). Neither `read_device_wall_ns()` nor `ensure_device_wall_buffer()` checks either gate — the only guard is `if (device_wall_dev_ptr_ == nullptr) return`, and the buffer is lazily allocated once and stays non-null. So with `SIMPLER_DEVICE_STRACE_ENABLE=0` all three transfers still happen every run and the data read back is discarded.

2. **The task-timing tail is opt-in per task but copied every run.** The tail (transfer #3, larger than the phase region on both arches) only holds data for tasks explicitly tagged via `set_task_timing_slot` (default `TASK_TIMING_SLOT_NONE`). Runs that tag no task — the common case — still pay the full tail D2H, reading back all-sentinel records.

Confirmed there is no other consumer of this data (no Python binding / benchmark return value reads it; grep of `python/bindings` is empty), so the readback exists purely to feed the strace markers.

This is per-run end-to-end latency on the dispatch/decode path, so it matters most on short-run, high-frequency workloads.

Verified on `upstream/main` at `a93a331fbfa2adfa02ea0e289cd61c08e20be2d5`.

### Location

- `src/common/platform/onboard/host/device_runner_base.cpp:1213` — `ensure_device_wall_buffer()` (per-run H2D reset)
- `src/common/platform/onboard/host/device_runner_base.cpp:1348` — `read_device_wall_ns()` (two D2H `rtMemcpy`, lines `1369` and `1407`)
- `src/a2a3/platform/onboard/host/device_runner.cpp:269` / `:619` — per-run call sites (a2a3)
- `src/a5/platform/onboard/host/device_runner.cpp:185` / `:442` — per-run call sites (a5)
- `src/common/platform/onboard/host/c_api_shared.cpp:470` — `device_profiling_enabled()` (env gate on the consumer)
- `src/common/platform/onboard/host/c_api_shared.cpp:484` — `emit_device_phase_markers()` (sole consumer of the readback)

### Priority

Low (no impact today, good to fix eventually)

title: Add: select A5 AICPU cores from runtime topology
body:
## Scope

This change adds topology-aware AICPU core selection for A5.

The runtime combines the authoritative device-side AICPU scheduler pool with Host CPU_TOPO metadata, classifies known FG, PG1, and PG2 topologies, and applies scenario placement for every supported active thread count from 2 through 5. Scheduler SMT availability is recorded as an independent topology property; it does not define a separate FG scenario.

A5 now supports at most five active AICPU threads. The independent launch population remains capped at 14 so the affinity gate can cover the device-visible scheduler pool.

## Changes

- Query device-side OCCUPY, PF_OCCUPY, and OS_SCHED before normal AICPU work.
- Prefer driver CPU_TOPO metadata and lock Host/AICPU wire layouts with compile-time ABI assertions.
- Match packaged fallback entries by SoC and every constraint declared by that entry. Ascend950PR_9599 requires exact OCCUPY `0x1f8` on either Host architecture; Ascend950PR_9579 also constrains Host architecture.
- Apply parameterized FG, PG1, and PG2 placement to manual and automatic active counts from 2 through 5.
- For UNKNOWN topology, use topology order when metadata is valid and CPU-ID order for OCCUPY-only metadata. Manual counts must be satisfied exactly; automatic mode may shrink from five but keeps at least one Scheduler and one Orchestrator.
- Keep explicitly generic verified fallbacks on the generic topology-aware packer.
- Cache successful merged topology probes for one DeviceRunner lifetime and invalidate them on recovery, reset, and finalize.
- Keep Runtime, DFX, affinity, and actual launch-count state consistent.
- Extend `aicpu-device-query` with A5 classification and diagnostic JSON output.
- Update design, hardware, runtime, and DFX documentation to the five-thread cap.

## Verification

- Final code review: passed with no remaining findings.
- `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD`: passed.
- C++ unit tests: 80/80 passed; A5 topology/selection target contains 23 tests.
- A5 onboard Host/AICPU/AICore builds passed for both `host_build_graph` and `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`.
- `aicpu-device-query` Host build passed.

title: [Feature] Raise CHIP_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS above 128 for composed L2 callables
body:
## Summary

Raise the chip-level tensor argument capacity from 128 to at least 192, or
replace the fixed cap with scalable/configurable storage, so that realistic
composed L2 callables can be dispatched without artificial splitting.

This is a follow-up to #786 / #788, which raised the previous limit from 64 to
128.

## Motivation

While composing the DeepSeek V4 MTP decode path into a single L2 callable, the
combined entry needs 164 tensor parameters:

1. main-model decode;
2. device-side MTP verification and token packing;
3. MTP draft decode.

The generated callable fails during startup with:

```text
ValueError: make_callable: sig_count exceeds MaxSig
```

The current limit is:

```cpp
inline constexpr int CHIP_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS = 128;
```

Because 164 exceeds this limit, the downstream implementation had to retain two
L2 submissions:

- L2 1: main decode + MTP verification/packing;
- L2 2: MTP draft decode.

Downstream references:

- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib/pull/884
- https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-serving/pull/133

The validated 3-to-2 L2 reduction lowered steady critical-rank host decode time
from 45.159 ms to 42.980 ms. Supporting a single L2 would allow us to evaluate
removing the remaining dispatch, bind, runner and output-validation boundary.
No additional latency improvement is claimed until a comparable 2-to-1
benchmark is available.

## Requested change

Please consider one of the following:

1. raise `CHIP_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS` to at least 192, leaving some headroom above the
   current 164-argument reproducer; or
2. make chip-level argument storage scalable or configurable so smaller models
   do not pay the maximum fixed-storage cost.

The change should cover all storage and transport points derived from the cap,
including:

- `ChipCallable::signature_`;
- `ChipStorageTaskArgs`;
- runtime `L2TaskArgs`;
- Python `make_callable` bindings;
- hierarchical-worker mailbox sizing and its capacity `static_assert`;
- relevant a2a3/a5 and sim/onboard paths.

Please also add a regression test that accepts a 164-tensor callable and rejects
`CHIP_MAX_TENSOR_ARGS + 1` with an error containing both the requested and
supported tensor counts.

## Capacity considerations

`Tensor` is currently 128 bytes, so raising the fixed capacity from 128 to 192
adds approximately 8 KiB to each fixed tensor-argument storage object.

The hierarchical-worker mailbox is currently 32 KiB and is statically sized to
hold the maximum accepted `TaskArgs` blob. A 192-tensor capacity may still fit,
but the complete layout including `CallConfig`, scalar arguments, headers,
alignment and the error region should be verified. A 256-tensor choice would
likely require a larger mailbox or out-of-line argument storage.

## Expected behavior

A composed callable with 164 tensor parameters should compile, upload and
dispatch successfully on supported a2a3/a5 sim and onboard runtimes, without
requiring a model-specific argument-packing workaround or an extra L2 boundary.

title: [Docs] host_build_graph docs and comments describe a runtime model the code no longer implements
body:
### Documentation Location

`host_build_graph` (a2a3). Verified against `upstream/main` @ `810fbcd117ac92a1ff0412b3c29fda12c2c1d01e`.

- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/docs/SCALAR_DATA_ACCESS.md` — §1, §3.2 (L44), §4 table (L109), §5 (L123)
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/docs/RUNTIME_LOGIC.md` — L300 (Sizing guideline), L362
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/orchestration/pto_orchestration_api.h` — L313
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/pto_runtime2_types.h` — L148
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_runtime2.cpp` — L110
- `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp` — L423

### What's Wrong or Missing?

`host_build_graph`'s documentation and several load-bearing code comments still describe a runtime model the code no longer implements. Three separate facets, all pre-existing on `main`.

---

#### 1. Removed dependency mechanism (`fanout_refcount`) is still presented as current behavior

The wiring/refcount dependency model was replaced by the polling model (`completion_flags` + `completed_watermark`). The refcount fields are gone — `fanout_refcount`, `fanin_refcount`, `fanout_head`, `fanout_count`, and `PTO2_FANOUT_SCOPE_BIT` have **zero field declarations** anywhere under `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/`, yet **34 references** to them remain.

Most are correct historical notes ("on_task_release is gone under polling… that signal is now the per-ring `completed_watermark`", `pto_scheduler.h:878`) and read fine. The following seven, however, state a removed mechanism as present-tense fact:

| Location | Text | Actual mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCALAR_DATA_ACCESS.md:44` | "wait for all consumers to finish (`fanout_refcount >= fanout_count - 1`, excluding the scope reference)" | `completed_watermark > last_consumer_local_id` |
| `SCALAR_DATA_ACCESS.md:109` | table row: "spin-wait fanout_refcount" | same as above |
| `SCALAR_DATA_ACCESS.md:123` | "INOUT registers a producer entry in TensorMap, enabling `set_tensor_data` to track all consumers through `fanout_refcount`" | same as above |
| `pto_orchestration_api.h:313` | "INOUT creates a TensorMap entry that enables automatic consumer tracking via `fanout_refcount`" | same as above |
| `pto_runtime2_types.h:148` | state machine: `COMPLETED->CONSUMED: fanout_refcount == fanout_count && state == COMPLETED` | no refcount participates |
| `pto_runtime2.cpp:110` | file-header comment: "(consumer low bits of `fanout_refcount` >= consumer count, excluding the …)" | same as above |
| `pto_orchestrator.cpp:423` | lists zeroed fields including `fanout_refcount=0` | field does not exist |

`pto_orchestration_api.h` is the header orchestration authors read directly, so a reader can reasonably act on L313.

---

#### 2. `SCALAR_DATA_ACCESS.md` §1 states a capability `host_build_graph` does not have

> During task graph construction, orchestration sometimes needs to **read InCore kernel results (for control-flow decisions)** or write initial values into tensors.

That is true for `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`, whose orchestrator runs on the AICPU concurrently with the schedulers. It is **not** true for `host_build_graph`: `run_host_orchestration()` runs the whole orchestration on the host, then `copy_to_device()` uploads the populated SM, and only then does the AICPU kernel boot scheduler-only (`aicpu_executor.cpp` — "host_build_graph has no device-side orchestrator"). No device task has executed during orchestration, so a producer's `task_state` can never reach `COMPLETED` and `wait_for_tensor_ready` spins to `PTO2_TENSOR_DATA_TIMEOUT_CYCLES` (15 s) before failing with `PTO2_ERROR_TENSOR_WAIT_TIMEOUT`.

The restriction is currently recorded only in a scene-test comment — `tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/available_aicore_counts/kernels/orchestration/available_aicore_counts_orch.cpp:75-79`:

```cpp
// shape carries no producer or consumer task, so set_tensor_data writes it
// straight through. Giving it one would hang host_build_graph: its
// orchestrator runs to completion on the host before the device executes
// anything, so a producer's task_state can never reach COMPLETED and
// wait_for_tensor_ready would spin to PTO2_TENSOR_DATA_TIMEOUT_CYCLES.
```

Both `host_build_graph` users of these APIs (`available_aicore_counts`, `paged_attention`) only touch tensors with no producer, which is the path that works. A reader who follows §1 instead gets a failure that surfaces 15 s later under an error code that does not point at the root cause. The doc lives under `host_build_graph/docs/` and carries no note of this difference.

---

#### 3. `RUNTIME_LOGIC.md` sizing guideline is scoped per-`PTO2_SCOPE`, and quotes a default that does not match the code

L300:

> **Sizing guideline**: `task_window_size` must be larger than the maximum number of tasks in any single `PTO2_SCOPE`. A safe choice is `2 × max_tasks_per_scope` or simply the default 65536 for production.

Two problems:

- **Scope of the constraint.** `host_build_graph` is whole-graph-resident and never advances `last_task_alive` (`pto_scheduler.h:26` — "reclaim (whole-graph-resident), so `last_task_alive` is not advanced here"). The ring allocator's gate is `local_task_id_ - last_alive + 1 < window_size_` (`pto_ring_buffer.h:145`); with `last_alive` pinned at 0 that becomes `local_task_id_ + 1 < window_size_`, so the effective cap is the **total task count of the whole graph**, not the largest scope. Sizing by `2 × max_tasks_per_scope` on a graph with many small scopes under-sizes the window, and the allocator then spins waiting for a reclaim that never happens.
- **Default value.** The doc says `65536` here and again at L362 (`task_window=65536`); the code is `#define PTO2_TASK_WINDOW_SIZE 16384` (`pto_runtime2_types.h:73`).

### Additional Context

- Found incidentally while reviewing #1618. **Everything above is pre-existing on `main` and independent of that PR** — no finding here is introduced by it.
- Only `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/` was swept. `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`, the top-level `docs/`, and `a5` were not checked and may carry similar residue from the same migration.
- Reproduce the residue counts with:

  ```bash
  for sym in fanout_refcount fanin_refcount fanout_head fanout_count PTO2_FANOUT_SCOPE_BIT; do
    printf '%-24s decls:%s refs:%s\n' "$sym" \
      "$(git grep -cE "(int32_t|uint32_t|uint64_t|std::atomic<[^>]*>)\s+$sym" -- src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/ | wc -l)" \
      "$(git grep -c "$sym" -- src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/ | awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END{print s+0}')"
  done
  ```

- Per `.claude/rules/doc-consistency.md`, doc updates are the responsibility of the commit that changes the code; that rule does not cover drift that already exists, which is why this is filed separately.

title: fix(a5): expose SPMD sub-retires in L2 swimlane
body:
## Summary

A5's `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` scheduler was missing the A2A3 `phase_subretire_count` DFX accounting. As a result, non-final SPMD FIN/retire events could be absent from Complete-phase records, and the profiling tools could conflate FIN counts with logical-task counts.

## Changes

- Port `phase_subretire_count` to the A5 scheduler and emit a Complete phase when either logical completions or non-final SPMD retires were observed.
- Preserve the runtime FIN/retire count in Chrome traces while retaining finish-row attribution for diagnostics.
- Update scheduler overhead analysis to report logical tasks and FINs separately.
- Document the `tasks_processed` semantics for Complete phases.
- Add Python regression tests and extend the A5 mixed-workload swimlane validation to check the expected FIN count.

## Scope

This is a DFX/profiling-accounting fix. Normal scheduling semantics are unchanged when DFX is disabled.

## Validation

- A5 sim runtime build (host, AICPU, and AICore): passed.
- Focused converter and scheduler-overhead tests: 33 passed.
- Commit hooks: clang-format, clang-tidy, cpplint, markdownlint, Ruff, and Pyright passed.

title: Test: prove the sim runner publishes launch acceptance
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing regression barrier for launch-acceptance publication on sim.

**This PR started as the strict-symbol-loading refactor and has been narrowed to
the test.** #1587 merged as `2a650f2d` while this was open and landed the whole
refactor independently — all four symbols strict, `load_optional_symbol`
deleted, the sim `set_task_accepted_state_ctx` export, the dead nullptr guards
removed, and the header docs updated. I verified main against my diff
line-by-line and it is equivalent throughout, so I dropped my `src/` changes
wholesale on rebase rather than churn a mechanism that had already shipped.

The one difference in approach: for `get_pipeline_contract` — absent from a5's
runtime makers — I had put a **weak depth-1 default in both platform
`c_api_shared.cpp`**, matching `prewarm_config_impl`; main instead added
**strong definitions to a5's two `runtime_maker.cpp`**. Both give a5 the
depth-1 contract, main's is explicit at the cost of the literal appearing in
two more places, and I checked a5's `host_build_graph` definition sits inside
`extern "C" {` so its linkage is right. Main's version stands.

## What is left, and why it is worth landing

Nothing asserted the accepted word ever **arrives**. The two endpoint scene
tests that read it (`worker_async_endpoint`, `worker_async_fifo`) assert it is
still `0` before activation — the negative direction — and both are
a2a3-onboard-only, so the sim side of the binding had no coverage at all.

That gap hid a real defect until #1587. The sim c_api exported no
`set_task_accepted_state_ctx`, so ChipWorker's then-optional load produced
`nullptr`, both bind sites were skipped, and `SimDeviceRunnerBase::publish_task_accepted`
found a null target. A sim child therefore never published acceptance, and the
run-level fence — `LocalMailboxEndpoint::read_task_accepted` → `on_accept` →
`Orchestrator::mark_task_accepted` → `decrement_run_accepts` — advanced only
once the run reached a terminal phase, because `acceptance_ready()` was
satisfied by its other disjunct. The launch fence silently degraded into a
completion fence on every sim run.

`worker.py` passes the accepted-word address on every platform (single-frame
`run_from_blob` and two-frame `_launch_native_run`, neither platform-gated), and
the sim runner does reach `publish_task_accepted()` at its launch boundary — so
this was never "sim doesn't use the accepted word", only an unexported symbol.

The test dispatches one ChipTask and asserts the word is set in whichever
mailbox frame carried it. That holds on both endpoint shapes because the parent
clears the word only when it publishes the next task into that frame, so it
survives completion.

**Verified to actually catch the regression:** against the pre-#1587 sim c_api
it fails with

```
E  AssertionError: the chip worker never published launch acceptance: [0, 0, 0]
E  assert 1 in [0, 0, 0]
```

## Testing

At the rebased base (`2a650f2d`):

- a2a3sim — this test: passed
- a2a3 onboard via `task-submit` (`task_20260803_010730_25475769728`, 1 device) — this test: **passed on real silicon**
- pre-commit on the changed file: all hooks passed

From the pre-rebase run of the full refactor (superseded by #1587, but the test
was present throughout): cpput 74/74 · pyut 1034 passed / 9 skipped · a2a3sim
sweep 63 PASS 0 FAIL · a5sim sweep 47 PASS 0 FAIL · a2a3 onboard sweep 62 PASS
0 FAIL before the run hit the 600 s `--pto-session-timeout` budget in its last
group on this shared box.
