title: CI: move redundant scene tests to daily sweep
body:
## Summary

- Reduce Per-PR scene-test cost by moving redundant smoke, scale-only,
  timing/DFX-observation, P4 collective, and selected duplicate Sim cases
  behind the existing manual selection.
- Keep `--manual exclude` as the reusable workflow default for PR CI; the
  separate Daily workflow uses `--manual include` to retain the full corpus.
- Extend manual selection to standalone pytest tests and platform-scoped
  markers, and pass the same mode to pre-compilation so only selected test
  classes are compiled.
- Validate `manual_mode` as `exclude`, `include`, or `only` before using it in
  shell commands.
- Keep case parameters, kernels, golden checks, tolerances, runtime settings,
  and workflow timeout thresholds unchanged.

## Per-PR coverage policy

Cases are moved out of Per-PR when their value is primarily shallow smoke,
rank/shape scale expansion, performance/marker observation, or a duplicate
execution path with a stronger representative still running. Per-PR retains
production-model paths, fault/recovery/stress coverage, large pressure cases,
and representative algorithm coverage on each supported platform.

Paged-attention shapes are unchanged, and A2/A3 Sim still retains the
500-task BGEMM pressure case.

## Cases removed from Per-PR

### Single-card and observability cases

| Test | Per-PR platforms removed | Coverage retained in Per-PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_hello_worker` | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard, A5 Sim, A5 Onboard | Worker allocation/copy/free and close paths |
| `test_vector_add` | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard | Other runtime vector computation paths |
| `TestMatmulHostBuildGraph::default` | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard | Graph record/replay path exercising the same incore kernels |
| `TestFaninLookupPerf` 64x64 cases | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard, A5 Sim, A5 Onboard | Dependency-generation boundary and representative fanout/fanin cases |
| `TestDummyTask::LongDummyChain` | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard, A5 Sim, A5 Onboard | Smaller dependency-chain and dense fanout/fanin cases |
| TMR/HBG vector examples | A2/A3 Sim, A5 Sim | Same cases remain Onboard; stronger computation paths remain on Sim |
| Graph execution 1D | A2/A3 Sim | Graph execution 2D remains on Sim; 1D remains Onboard |
| BGEMM 64 | A2/A3 Sim | 500-task `Case0` remains on Sim; BGEMM 64 remains Onboard |
| Run-timing and task-timing marker tests | Supported Sim platforms | Onboard marker coverage and Per-PR vector correctness remain |
| `ffn_tp_parallel` | A2/A3 Sim, A5 Sim | Same two-card matmul + allreduce path remains A3 Onboard |
| `dual_domain_overlap` | A2/A3 Sim, A5 Sim | `domain_rank_map` remains on both Sim lanes; the full overlap computation remains A3 Onboard |

### Collective cases

| Tests | Per-PR platforms removed | Coverage retained in Per-PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Allgather, AllToAll, Broadcast, and ReduceScatter P4 | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard, A5 Sim | The corresponding P2 collective remains on both Sim lanes and A3 Onboard |
| Allreduce One-phase, Two-phase, Ring, and Bidirectional Ring P4; Ibing four-rank error | A2/A3 Sim, A3 Onboard, A5 Sim | One-phase and Ring P2 remain on both Sim lanes; all five P2 algorithms remain on A3 and A5 Onboard |
| Allreduce Two-phase, Bidirectional Ring, and Ibing P2 | A2/A3 Sim, A5 Sim | One-phase and Ring P2 remain on both Sim lanes; all five P2 algorithms remain on A3 and A5 Onboard |

A5 Onboard is unchanged by the P4 migration because the P4 classes are not
defined for that platform. Daily continues to run every migrated P2 and P4
case on its supported platforms.

## CI compatibility fixes

- The profiling-flags smoke targets a vector example that is now manual on Sim,
  so it explicitly passes `--manual include`; otherwise pytest deselects the
  only target and exits non-zero.
- All four reusable Sim/Onboard workflows validate `manual_mode` through an
  environment variable before shell parsing, then reuse only the validated
  value in pytest, pre-compile, and `task-submit --run` commands.
- No-hardware C++ UT builds use four-way CMake build parallelism to avoid the
  macOS serial-build tail that previously exhausted the 20-minute job timeout.

## Validation

- Targeted profiling smoke target passed on A2/A3 Sim and A5 Sim.
- Collective selection checks verify every P4 class is manual, while the three
  additional P2 cases are manual only on the two Sim platforms.
- `python -m pytest tests/ut/py/test_scene_level_selection.py -q`: 8 passed.
- Targeted pre-commit checks passed for the changed Python, YAML, Markdown, and
  repository policy files.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`: passed.

title: [Performance] A2A3 fresh AICore stream per run regresses repeated HCA/SWA Effective latency by 3.8–4.4%
body:
## Background

In pypto-lib, repeated same-image DeepSeek-V4 Flash HCA/SWA execution on
`a2a3` with the `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` runtime has a performance
regression at Simpler PR #1540: median `effective_us` increases by 3.81–4.36%.

Repro cases:

- `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_hca.py`
- `models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_swa.py`

Both entrypoints and their helpers are public at pypto-lib
`1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863` on `main`. The test also applies
the public pypto-lib commit `c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42`,
which only migrates 17 `valid_shapes` keyword arguments to `valid_shape`.

Reproduction environment:

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| pypto-lib | `1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863` + compatibility patch `c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42` (`main`) |
| PyPTO | `2e59c01ccc34e586e19b49ecaa1a94b2e21db459` (`main`) |
| Simpler baseline | `8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd` (detached) |
| Simpler regressing commit | `e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717` (detached) |
| PTOAS | `0.54` |
| PTO ISA | `83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |
| Driver / Ascend HAL | `26.0.rc1` / `7.35.23` |
| Python | `3.10.19` |

Controlled A/B note: PyPTO `2e59c01c` records Simpler `dccb8379`. To isolate
PR #1540, the runtime checkout was intentionally overridden with the PR parent
and PR commit above. PTOAS and PTO ISA remained fixed. A separate pin-consistent
PyPTO runtime-bundle A/B independently showed the same regression direction and
magnitude.

Diagnosis: **simpler** — the direct Simpler parent/commit A/B reproduces the
regression while pypto-lib, PyPTO, PTOAS, PTO ISA, model inputs, and benchmark
settings remain fixed.

### Platform

`a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C hardware)`

### Runtime Variant

`tensormap_and_ringbuffer`

### Summary

Simpler PR #1540 changes the A2/A3 runner from retaining an AICore stream for
repeated runs of the same image to creating and retiring a fresh AICore stream
for every run. A direct parent/commit A/B on DeepSeek-V4 Flash HCA and SWA shows
median `effective_us` regressions of 4.36% and 3.81%, respectively.

Each endpoint used 5 warmups followed by 100 measured iterations. All four
runs passed `kv_cache` and `x_out` validation.

### Git Commit ID

`e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`

### CANN Version

`9.0.0`

### Driver Version

`26.0.rc1` (Ascend HAL `7.35.23`)

### Host Platform

`Linux (aarch64)` — Huawei Cloud EulerOS 2.0, kernel
`5.10.0-182.0.0.95.r1941_123.hce2.aarch64`

### Reproduction

Use isolated checkouts and a separate virtual environment for each Simpler
endpoint.

```bash
git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> checkout \
  1f48761cb5be21a8cf0611fad10d513ba40b0863

git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> show --format= \
  c0751b7582618f7ccef29385236b1964cb480d42 \
  -- models/deepseek/v4-flash/hc_pre.py | \
  git -C <pypto-lib-checkout> apply -

git -C <pypto-checkout> checkout \
  2e59c01ccc34e586e19b49ecaa1a94b2e21db459
git -C <pypto-checkout> submodule update --init --recursive

git -C <pypto-checkout>/runtime checkout <runtime-revision>
git -C <pto-isa-checkout> checkout \
  83d01313d9bfc247c4b7c8bcf969d1019f0d106f

source <CANN-root>/set_env.sh
export PTO_ISA_ROOT=<pto-isa-checkout>

python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e <pypto-checkout>
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e <pypto-checkout>/runtime

task-submit --ptoas 0.54 --device 4 --timeout 0 --max-time 1800 --run '
cd <pypto-lib-checkout>
export PYPTO_BENCH=1
export PYPTO_BENCH_WARMUP=5
export PYPTO_BENCH_ROUNDS=100
export PYPTO_BENCH_RAW=1
export PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=262144
export PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=262144
export PTO2_RING_HEAP=2147483648
export PYPTO_RUNTIME_LOG=error

python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_hca.py \
  -p a2a3 -d "$TASK_DEVICE" \
  --start-pos 8192 --enable-l2-swimlane 0

python models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_attention_swa.py \
  -p a2a3 -d "$TASK_DEVICE" \
  --start-pos 8192 --enable-l2-swimlane 0
'
```

Run once with baseline runtime
`8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd`, then repeat with
`e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`.

### Expected Performance

With parent commit `8e00319e28cd2ea9f7f7f795a2b1e182956b91bd`:

| Case | Median `effective_us` |
| --- | ---: |
| HCA | 259.2 us |
| SWA | 244.0 us |

Repeated same-image execution should retain this steady-state latency after
warmup while preserving correctness when different images alternate.

### Actual Performance

With PR #1540 commit `e51c3aeecfaf982137b6adc67ca13749b0c95717`:

| Case | Median `effective_us` | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HCA | 270.5 us | +11.3 us / +4.36% |
| SWA | 253.3 us | +9.3 us / +3.81% |

Test window: 2026-08-11 19:05:39–19:10:05 UTC+8. One 100-round batch was
run per endpoint/case. A separate PyPTO runtime-bundle boundary A/B produced
HCA +12.5 us and SWA +8.7 us, independently corroborating the result.

### Profiling Data (Optional)

Before PR #1540, `ensure_run_stream_set(slot, aicore_image_hash)` returns
immediately when the retained AICore stream carries the same image hash. The
5 warmups and 100 measured rounds therefore share one AICore stream.

After PR #1540:

- `RunStreamSlots::acquire()` always creates a fresh AICore stream.
- The stream is retired after every completed run.
- The 5-warmup/100-round benchmark therefore uses 105 fresh AICore streams.

The reported `effective_us` metric is the on-device merged orch/sched window.
Host-side `rtStreamCreate` occurs before that device window, and
`rtStreamDestroy` occurs after device completion and timing readback. The
9–11 us regression is therefore not direct host stream API latency.

Generated AICore binaries are unchanged across the direct A/B:

| Case | Byte-identical child binaries | Regression per child |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| HCA | 35/35 | 0.323 us |
| SWA | 28/28 | 0.332 us |

The strongest current explanation is a device-side cold-start effect: using a
fresh stream for every same-image run prevents retention of prior
instruction-fetch/I-cache/stream-affinity state. The commit boundary and stream
lifecycle change are proven; PMU `icache_req`/`icache_miss` data or a
stream-only toggle is still needed to confirm the exact hardware mechanism.

### Additional Context

The fresh-stream policy was introduced for correctness when different images
are published to the same GM code address. A plain restoration of the old
per-slot image-hash cache may reintroduce stale-instruction risk for an
`A -> B -> A` sequence across depth-two slots.

A safer remediation direction is runner-wide, generation-aware same-image
reuse: reuse only for consecutive identical images when no overlapping code
range has been republished, and recreate the stream when image identity or code
address generation changes. Stable non-overlapping code banks or a supported
AICore instruction-cache invalidation operation are alternatives.

Acceptance should cover repeated same-image performance, alternating-image
correctness, depth-two slot alternation, and stream-creation counts.

Source inspection of Simpler `main` at
`c5a587400721ea98f0a00321569088a5321539b9` shows that
`RunStreamSlots::acquire()` still unconditionally creates a fresh AICore stream.
The numerical A/B above was performed at the PR parent/commit, not at that
latest-main commit.

Related: #1717 discusses hiding per-run device launch latency and persistent
execution for `host_build_graph`; this report concerns repeated same-image
device Effective regression in `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`.

title: [Code Health] Log subsystem — one clock, one grammar, one gate
body:
### Category

Technical Debt (cleanup, refactor)

### Component

Host Runtime

### Description

The `[STRACE]` logging substrate underneath the DFX timelines has accumulated
duplicated ownership. Reviewing #1730 surfaced six specific divergences; each is
small, but together they mean the record channel has no single owner for its
clock, its identity fields, its grammar, or its gate.

Decided by reference to the atrace/ftrace model, which #1708 already cites as the
architectural precedent — we copied its *channel* design ("the runtime emits,
tooling renders, the caller is untouched") but not its *clock* design, and there
was no reason for that omission.

**Status, updated 2026-08-17.** Items 1 and 2 landed with #1730 (`9693545d`).
Item 4 is implemented by #1845, which is also where items 4 and 7 below were
corrected against a real implementation. Items 3, 5, 6 and 7 remain open.

**1. One clock.** ✅ Landed in #1730. A record used to carry two times: a
wall-clock stamp in the prefix (`system_clock` + `localtime_r` + `strftime`,
which jumps on NTP correction) and a monotonic time inside the span payload.
They were not comparable, so the envelope could not order records. It is now
one — the prefix carries monotonic ns, and each process emits a single
`clock_anchor` record at startup mapping monotonic to wall clock, so absolute
time stays recoverable. `strace_timing.py` applies that mapping to `--trace-out`
and `--swimlane` as of #1845.

The anchor is at `TIMING`, not `INFO`: the gate is `level >= current_level_` and
the default threshold is `TIMING` (25), so an `INFO` (20) anchor would be
suppressed exactly when spans are present.

**2. The log fills in who and when; the caller says what.** ✅ Landed in #1730.
`strace.h` used to call `getpid()` itself and hand-write the
`[STRACE] v=1 pid=… tid=…` line while `host_log.cpp` wrote a second copy with a
different `inv` conversion (`%u` vs `%llu`). There is now one owner and one
format string.

**3. Ask before you build.** ⬆️ **Promoted from optimization to necessary by
#1845.** The attribute string is formatted unconditionally and only then may the
record be discarded for being below the threshold, so lowering the log level buys
nothing back. Expose a cheap `enabled(level)` query and check it at the call
site.

Two facts raise the priority. First, the measured cost is ~3.34 µs per record on
a pipe (~10 µs per task at current span density), of which only about half is
recoverable by lowering the level — the rest is the encode that happens before
the gate. Second, #1845 deletes the only short-circuit that existed:
`host_span_scope.h::emit()` used to open with `if (sink == nullptr) return;`, so
a build without a logger paid nothing. Nothing replaces it, and
`_host_spans_active()` collapsed to a bare `HOST_STRACE_ENABLED`. The call order
is now unconditionally validate → `encode_host_span_field(name)` →
`encode_host_span_field(attributes)` → `log()` → `vlog()` → `is_enabled()`: two
heap allocations ahead of the level check, on every span, with no runtime way to
opt out.

**4. Stop shipping the logger as a separately-resolved artifact.** ✅ Implemented
by #1845. It was reached by runtime `dlopen`, which is what forced the binding
machinery in #1730. Compiling it into each consumer and sharing only *state* by
pointer at each module's init makes a missing logger impossible rather than a
state to handle.

Two corrections to how this item was originally written, both found by reviewing
the implementation:

- **The shared-state set is `(threshold, clock_anchor_pid, drop counter)`, not
  `(threshold, drop counter)`.** The original wording missed that duplicating the
  *code* is what turns "one `[CLOCK_ANCHOR]` per process" into shared mutable
  state. With a single instance that invariant was free — `clock_anchor_pid_` was
  just a member of the singleton. With N copies it needs a protocol to restore
  (#1845 uses `0 → -pid` to claim, `-pid → +pid` to publish, `-pid → 0` to
  release on write failure). This is the design's omission, not an
  implementation liberty.
- **"the same mechanism the silicon side already uses" was wrong and is
  withdrawn.** The silicon side passes an integer *by value* through an existing
  init ABI — `init_args.log_level = HostLogger::get_instance().level()` in
  `device_runner_base.cpp`, and `set_log_level(int)` on the sim AICPU. That is
  precisely the mechanism that causes the push-once defect recorded at the bottom
  of this issue, so it is the wrong precedent to have cited. A shared pointer
  with an ABI version/size handshake is heavier but strictly better here, and it
  is what #1845 built.

Two properties #1845 established that this item did not ask for, recorded so they
are not lost:

- Hiding every symbol except one binder (`visibility("hidden")` on `HostLogger`
  and the `unified_log_*` definitions, one default-visibility
  `simpler_host_log_bind_state`) is what actually prevents regressing to a global
  singleton through ELF interposition. Sharing state by pointer alone would not.
- Removing the `RTLD_GLOBAL` logger also removed the reason
  `-undefined dynamic_lookup` existed on three macOS targets.

**5. Fold sim's device log in.** Sim's "device" is simulation: it runs on the host
CPU in the same process, yet it has its own writer, its own envelope
(`[<LEVEL>] <func>: ` — no timestamp, no thread id) and its own copy of the
≤`PIPE_BUF` single-write rule. Only the real-silicon logger genuinely cannot
share the sink.

That single-write invariant being derived twice, in two implementations that
write the same stderr, is the sharpest instance of the general problem: a drift
in either copy tears records, and torn records are silently dropped by
`parse_spans`. **The drift is real and currently present.** `host_log.cpp`
budgets a span record to `_POSIX_PIPE_BUF` (512) and enforces it with a
`static_assert`; `sim/aicpu/device_log.cpp` caps its record at 2048 bytes and
justifies that against "Linux PIPE_BUF (4096)", with no assertion. macOS's
`PIPE_BUF` is 512, so the sim copy's stated justification does not hold on a
platform CI runs. Whether a current call site emits more than 512 bytes is
unverified; the defect is that the bound is stated against the wrong constant and
is unenforced. #1851 corrected the *test's* comment to `_POSIX_PIPE_BUF` and left
the implementation's at Linux's value, so the two now disagree in-tree.

Note on sequencing: #1845 adds a `set_host_log_state` / `get_host_log_state`
relay to that file under `SIMPLER_CPU_SIM_HOST_LOG_BRIDGE` so the sim AICPU SO
can hand shared state to a subsequently loaded orchestration SO. The file
therefore gained a host-log dependency without losing its duplicate writer,
which makes this item slightly larger than before rather than smaller.

**6. Never block; drop and count.** ftrace drops and counts on a full buffer and
never stalls the producer. Our channel is a shared fd, so `O_NONBLOCK` is not
available (it would change behaviour for Python's own `sys.stderr`). Staged: add
the drop counter for the failure paths that already exist, measure whether a
write ever actually blocks, and build a bounded queue only if a number justifies
it. Recording the requirement now prevents a later "fix" that adds a sleep to the
dispatch path, which codestyle §5 forbids.

Three updates:

- **"Measure whether a write ever actually blocks" has an answer: yes.** #1851
  fixed a deadlock in `test_sim_device_log` where writers filled a capture pipe
  and blocked in `write(2)` while the only reader waited for them. Any consumer
  that captures our stderr through a pipe and does not drain it promptly stalls
  the dispatch path. This is no longer hypothetical.
- **The process-wide write mutex no longer exists.** After #1845 each DSO has its
  own `HostLogger::mutex_`. This *reduces* blocking amplification — a stalled
  write no longer holds up every host writer in the process — and *increases*
  tearing exposure, because cross-module atomicity now rests solely on the single
  ≤`PIPE_BUF` `write(2)`. That holds for `[STRACE]` (`static_assert(... <=
  _POSIX_PIPE_BUF - 256)`) but not for ordinary records: `kRecordStackCapacity`
  is 2048 and its own comment says "This capacity is not an atomic-write
  guarantee", and above it there is an unbounded `std::vector<char>` path.
- **#1845 does not add the drop counter** despite its PR body and commit message
  claiming it does. `write_stderr` was changed to return `bool`, but the only
  consumer of that value is the anchor claim/release. This item's first stage is
  therefore still entirely open.

**7. Decide what a module logs before it is bound.** New, and a direct
consequence of item 4. Between a module's `dlopen` and its
`simpler_host_log_bind_state` call it filters against its own
`g_module_log_state`, which #1845 defaults to `TIMING`. The original item 4 never
specified this state; the implementation picked a value silently. Three options:

- **(a) default `TIMING`** (what shipped) — an unbound module logs at the default
  threshold regardless of the process setting, so a missed binding shows up as
  *wrong-level output*, which nobody notices.
- **(b) default `NUL`** — an unbound module is silent, so a missed binding shows
  up as *a module with no records at all*, which is visible in a log.
- **(c) refuse and count** — needs item 6's counter first.

(b) is preferred: it converts a class of loader bug from silently-wrong into
observably-absent. Today nothing depends on the choice — `grep -rn
'__attribute__((constructor))' src/` is empty and `TIMING` happens to equal the
documented default — but the decision should be explicit rather than incidental.

### Location

- `src/common/log/host_log.cpp` — envelope, the `PIPE_BUF` premise, the anchor
  claim protocol, per-module `mutex_`
- `src/common/log/include/common/host_log_state.h` — the shared-state ABI
  (item 4's actual field set)
- `src/common/log/include/common/host_span_scope.h` — item 3's call site: where a
  cheap `enabled()` gate belongs, and where the deleted short-circuit was
- `src/common/platform/sim/aicpu/device_log.cpp` — the parallel writer, envelope
  and atomicity copy; also the `SIMPLER_CPU_SIM_HOST_LOG_BRIDGE` relay
- `python/simpler/_log.py`, `python/simpler/task_interface.py` — threshold
  propagation

### Proposed Fix

The open items in order: **3** (cheap `enabled()` gate at the call site), then
**7** (the unbound-window default, one line but it belongs in the same change as
3), then **5** (fold sim's writer in, fixing the 2048-vs-512 drift on the way),
then **6** (drop counter first, bounded queue only if measured).

**Item 5 must not be started while #1845 is in flight** — that PR already
restructures `sim/aicpu/device_log.cpp` and is where the sim-side host-log
plumbing lands.

Item 3 should land before the span rename tracked in #1793, for the same reason
item 2 did: gating one emit site is far easier than gating three.

### Related defect, partially resolved

**The threshold fan-out was push-once.** `HostLogger::current_level_` was the
single C++ owner and both derived copies read it — sim's via
`sim/host/device_runner.cpp` and the onboard AICPU's via `init_args.log_level`,
both justified (RTLD_LOCAL, silicon boundary). But each was seeded once at init,
so changing the threshold afterwards reached nothing.

**Half fixed by #1845, and this is worth stating because #1845 does not claim
it.** Host-side modules now read `state()->threshold` on every record, so a
mid-run `set_level` reaches all of them. The device side is unchanged: onboard
AICPU still receives a one-shot `InitArgs.log_level` snapshot, so a threshold
change after device init still does not reach it. Any future "the log level is
now live" claim must scope itself to host modules.

The second defect recorded here — that the parent process's threshold was not
seeded at all, because `_initialize_simpler_log` had one caller inside the forked
child's `ChipWorker.init` — was fixed in #1730 as merged.

### Priority

Medium

title: [Code Health] Rename span families to pod/host/chip/core — coordinated across simpler, pypto-lib, pypto-serving
body:
### Category

Naming / Consistency

### Component

Other (please specify in description)

Affects the `[STRACE]` span vocabulary, which spans `src/common/`,
`simpler_setup/tools/`, the docs, and **two external repositories**.

### Description

Span names currently come in two unrelated families with no shared scheme, and one
of them is a de-facto contract with repositories outside this one.

Today:

| Family | Emitted by | Occurrences |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------- |
| `simpler_run*`, `simpler_prewarm.*` | the chip runtime in the forked child | ~185 in 37 files |
| `l3.*` | the L3 parent (added by #1730, unreleased) | ~59 in 17 files |

**The scheme.** One word per level of the hierarchy — the same levels, named
instead of numbered:

| Prefix | Level | What it describes | Replaces |
| ------ | ----- | ----------------- | -------- |
| `pod.` | L4 | a Worker whose children are L3 Workers | nothing emits it yet |
| `host.` | L3 | one host driving chips: graph build, submit, dispatch, worker threads | `l3.*` |
| `chip.` | L2 | the chip runtime in the forked child | `simpler_run*`, `simpler_prewarm.*` |
| `core.` | L0 | the in-core AIC/AIV pipeline | the core-swimlane tool's own output |

Numeric levels stay out of the names, consistent with codestyle rule 13's mapping
of L2 → `Chip` and L0 → `Core`. Rule 13 lumps L3+ together as *unprefixed* because
it governs type and identifier names, where one `Worker` serves every level above
the chip; a trace does need L3 distinguished from L4, hence two words where the rule
has none.

**The prefix is per process, not per call site.** `Orchestrator::submit_impl` and
`WorkerThread::submit_dispatch` are level-agnostic — the same code runs at L3 and
L4. It does not need to be per site: a Worker forks its next-level children into
separate processes, so one process hosts exactly one Worker level, and the prefix
resolves once at Worker init.

**Reserve a namespace for external producers.** `pod./host./chip./core.` are *our*
levels and a caller is not one of them; without a reserved prefix a caller's span
named `host.foo` parses as ours. Settle it here rather than when a public tracing
API lands, because this is the one moment every name and every parser is already
being touched.

### Location

Inside this repo:

- `simpler_setup/tools/strace_timing.py` — `legacy_spans()`, `_ROUNDS_TABLE_NAMES`,
  `_host_thread_name`, the swimlane process-role test, the flow-key pairing
- Hardcoded assertions that will fail loudly (good):
  `tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/native_run_lifecycle/test_native_run_lifecycle.py`
  (an expected-depth table), `tests/st/a5/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/bench_prewarm_timing.py`
  (a compiled regex on `name=simpler_run.bind.prebuilt`),
  `examples/workers/l2/vector_add/test_run_timing.py`, `tests/ut/py/test_strace_timing.py`
- Docs: `docs/dfx/host-trace.md`, `docs/dfx/l2-timing.md`, `docs/dfx/device-phases.md`,
  `simpler_setup/tools/README.md`, and the `dfx-analyze` / `benchmark` skills

Outside this repo — the reason this needs coordination rather than a rename commit:

- **pypto-lib** `pypto/runtime/bench.py` carries **its own copy** of the span-name
  table (`_ROUNDS_TABLE_NAMES`), and its comments still reference the
  `run_prepared` → `simpler_run` root rename from simpler #1210 — with the table
  still keyed off the **pre-#1210** spelling. `golden/runner.py` reuses that parser.
- **pypto-serving** `.agents/skills/qwen3-14b-offline-perf-test/SKILL.md` hardcodes
  `simpler_run`, `runner_run`, `device_wall` and the formula
  `simpler_run.runner_run.device_wall.graph_build` as `Effective`. Being a runbook,
  it fails **silently** — the agent simply stops finding the field.

`docs/dfx/host-trace.md` frames this as a feature: *"A consumer (e.g. pypto-serving)
reads the per-stage breakdown from the log, with no code change on its side and no
API contract."* "No API contract" is precisely the problem — the names *are* the
contract. #1210 already renamed a span root once, the downstream repo had to adapt,
and the scar is still in its code.

### Proposed Fix

Coordinated rename across simpler, pypto-lib and pypto-serving together — no
dual-spelling window and no alias table, so the retired spellings actually go away
rather than lingering the way #1210's did.

1. Settle the merge order. simpler emits the new names, so it lands last or behind
   something the other two can pin against; otherwise their parsers see unknown
   names for the window between merges.
2. Rename in simpler, and replace `legacy_spans()`'s allow-list with an explicit
   family split so per-task `host.*` spans stay out of the invocation-grouping path.
3. Downstream edits in the two files located above.
4. A grep gate per repo: zero occurrences of the retired spellings, **in prose as
   well as code**, since the pypto-serving consumer is a runbook.

Blocked on #1792's "one span entry point" item — renaming one emit site is far
easier than renaming three — and on the `by_name()` fix requested in #1730, because
removing the allow-list is what makes that latent bug live.

### Priority

Medium

title: [Feature] Public Python tracing API — let callers put their own spans on the host swimlane
body:
### Summary

Expose a small public Python tracing API so a caller can instrument **its own**
code onto the same timeline the host swimlane renders, instead of only reading the
spans we emit.

The plumbing already exists — `_task_interface._emit_host_span` is a private
seven-argument entry point today. What is missing is an ergonomic surface, a
reserved namespace, and a decision to treat the record format as a supported
contract.

### Motivation / Use Case

The concrete beneficiary is not hypothetical. **pypto-lib** today only *parses* our
output (`pypto/runtime/bench.py`'s `_parse_stats_from_strace`) and prints its own
phase timings in a separate format. If it could *write* into the same stream, its
phases would land on the same swimlane next to ours, on the same clock and in the
same lane structure.

That extends the "one timeline" property from our code to the caller's code, which
is the whole point of the host swimlane (#1708) — today the timeline stops at our
own boundary.

Secondary: end-user model code that wants to know which of its own phases overlap
device execution has no way to say so.

### Proposed API / Behavior

The OpenTelemetry / `TRACE_EVENT` idiom. Note that perfetto's Python package is not
the model here — it only builds and queries trace files and has no instrumentation
API.

```python
from simpler import trace

with trace.span("my_phase", batch=16, layer=3):
    ...

@trace.span("my_func")
def f(): ...

trace.instant("checkpoint", k=v)          # zero duration

if trace.enabled():                        # skip expensive attribute building
    trace.span("expensive", **compute_attrs())
```

Design points, each following from a decision already taken elsewhere:

- **The wrapper reads the clock itself**, so a caller never handles timestamps and
  the one-clock property holds by construction rather than by documentation.
- **Names are auto-prefixed with a reserved namespace**; a caller cannot land a span
  in `host.` / `chip.` / `pod.` / `core.`. Multiple external producers can coexist in
  one process (pypto-lib and a user script), so a per-application prefix is more
  useful than a single shared `user.`.
- **`inv` / `hid` stay out of the public surface** — they are our internal
  correlation keys (`run_id`, callable digest) and a caller has no meaningful value
  for them. Offer an optional opaque `correlate=` instead.
- **Attributes are kwargs** onto the open `k=v` payload, so a caller adding fields
  needs no format version bump.
- **`trace.enabled()` is public**, because a caller must be able to skip attribute
  construction on a hot path.
- **The record format becomes a versioned contract** at this point. The `v=1` field
  exists for exactly this; publishing the API is what turns the format from
  de-facto public into formally public.

### Alternatives Considered

- **Leave it private and let callers keep parsing our output.** That is the status
  quo, and it is why pypto-lib maintains a duplicate span-name table and its own
  timing printout. It also means a caller's phases can never appear on the same
  timeline.
- **Expose the existing seven-argument `_emit_host_span` as-is.** Rejected: it
  requires the caller to supply timestamps (so the one-clock property becomes a
  documentation request rather than a guarantee), and it leaks `inv` / `hid`.
- **Adopt an external tracing library (perfetto SDK, OpenTelemetry).** Rejected for
  the same reasons ftrace was rejected in #1708: a new dependency, a collector
  daemon, and a channel that is not the process stderr our consumers already
  capture at the fd level.

### Additional Context

Blocked on work tracked elsewhere, all of it already planned:

- #1792 — one clock, one span entry point, and a queryable `enabled()` gate. The
  API should call the one entry point rather than becoming a fourth grammar.
- #1793 — the reserved namespace for external producers, settled as part of the
  rename rather than bolted on afterwards.
- #1792's backpressure item is promoted from "later, if measured" to a
  **prerequisite** by this issue: once third parties can emit, the emission rate
  stops being ours to control, and a caller instrumenting a hot loop would load the
  same write path and the same mutex that our dispatch path uses.

**Sequencing constraint worth stating explicitly:** do not publish the API before
#1792's clock change lands. That change alters the record envelope; publishing first
would make the format a formal external contract immediately before changing it.
Today it is only a de-facto one.

Sub-issue of #995, alongside #1708.

title: [Docs] Align DFX CLI and chip-swimlane documentation with the current implementation
body:
### Documentation Location

- `docs/dfx/chip-swimlane-profiling.md` (multi-round behavior, record layouts, a2a3/a5 comparison, stale setter name)
- `docs/dfx/profiling-framework.md` (stale AICore setter name)
- `docs/testing.md` and `docs/user/reference/cli.md` ("first round only" contract)
- `conftest.py` and `simpler_setup/scene_test.py` (`--enable-dep-gen` help)
- Inline DFX comments in:
  - `src/{a2a3,a5}/runtime/*/aicore/aicore_executor.cpp`
  - `src/common/platform/include/common/chip_swimlane_profiling.h`

### What's Wrong or Missing?

Verified against `upstream/main` at `50c0660646217f1b56172a81990279bd066ed971`.
Several DFX descriptions no longer match the implementation:

1. **Multi-round behavior is described as first-round capture, but the pytest path disables DFX for the entire case.**
   - `SceneTestCase.test_run()` sets chip swimlane, args dump, PMU, dep-gen, and scope stats to disabled when `--rounds > 1`.
   - `run_class_cases()` passes those already-gated values through every round; it does not mask only rounds after round 0.
   - Despite that, `docs/dfx/chip-swimlane-profiling.md` says in several places that the first round records, `docs/testing.md` says profiling is enabled on the first round, and the dep-gen CLI/help text says "first round only".
   - The standalone path is not fully consistent with pytest: its multi-round gate omits PMU, and `_run_parallel_standalone()` does not forward `--enable-pmu` in the common child arguments. The intended contract therefore needs to be settled before the docs can state one behavior for both entry points.

2. **The documented AICore swimlane setter no longer exists.**
   - The implementation declares and calls `set_chip_swimlane_aicore_head_slot()`.
   - `set_aicore_chip_swimlane_ring` remains in `docs/dfx/chip-swimlane-profiling.md`, `docs/dfx/profiling-framework.md`, and three `aicore_executor.cpp` comments, but has no definition or declaration on current `main`.

3. **The phase-record architecture/size table is stale.**
   - `docs/dfx/chip-swimlane-profiling.md` describes a2a3 scheduler phase records as 40 B and a5 as a legacy unified 40 B record with a split-layout port pending.
   - Both architectures now consume the shared split types. `ChipSwimlaneAicpuSchedPhaseRecord` has a compile-time size assertion of 64 B and `ChipSwimlaneAicpuOrchPhaseRecord` is 32 B; both a2a3 and a5 define separate scheduler/orchestrator buffer counts.

4. **The phase-buffer capacity comment has incorrect arithmetic.**
   - `PLATFORM_PHASE_RECORDS_PER_THREAD == 16384`.
   - The scheduler record is 64 B, so its record payload is about 1 MiB per buffer/thread; the orchestrator record is 32 B, so it is about 512 KiB. The current comment says both are about 512 KiB.

These mismatches make the DFX docs unreliable as an implementation map and can cause users to expect artifacts from a multi-round run that the pytest harness deliberately suppresses.

### Suggested Improvement

- Decide and test one multi-round contract for pytest and standalone execution, including PMU forwarding/gating.
- Update all user-facing help and docs to state that exact contract; if the current pytest behavior is intended, say that DFX is disabled when `--rounds > 1`, not that only later rounds are skipped.
- Replace stale `set_aicore_chip_swimlane_ring` references with the current slot-based API and explain the lazy head resolution where relevant.
- Update the architecture comparison and record sizes to the shared split layout used by both a2a3 and a5.
- Correct the per-buffer payload arithmetic (64 B × 16384 ≈ 1 MiB for scheduler; 32 B × 16384 ≈ 512 KiB for orchestrator).
- Add a small CLI contract test for standalone child forwarding/multi-round gating so the two entry points cannot drift silently again.

### Additional Context

Related: #995 (DFX capability tracking umbrella).

This report is based on source/control-flow inspection; no runtime code was modified while auditing it.

title: [Bug] Scheduler can deadlock when blocking TWAIT tasks prevent producer progress
body:
## Summary

Simpler currently schedules tasks containing blocking `TWAIT` operations through
the same core-slot mechanism as ordinary run-to-completion tasks. A `TWAIT` task
can therefore enter the running state and occupy a non-preemptive core slot while
the task needed to satisfy its wait is still pending. This can introduce a
resource-dependency cycle and stop device-side progress.

In the workload where this was observed, adding the missing explicit dependencies
between the communication producers and waiters resolves the hang. Those
dependencies belong in the submitted task graph because the library is the layer
that knows the communication semantics. However, the incident also shows that
Simpler does not currently define or enforce a forward-progress contract for
blocking tasks: an incomplete dependency graph can become an opaque device hang,
and a task that intentionally waits after admission has no stated resource
guarantee.

## Deadlock mechanism

The submitted task graph can make both a waiter and its producer appear ready,
but their eventual core-slot placement adds a resource edge that is not visible
in the graph:

```text
waiter W is running on core C
        |
        | waits for a notification produced by P
        v
producer P is pending on core C
        |
        | waits for W to release C
        +------------------------------> W
```

The same mechanism can span devices: a local waiter may require a remote
producer, while that producer is prevented from running by another blocking
waiter. The task DAG alone does not expose the resulting global resource cycle.

## Observed behavior

The failure is timing- and placement-sensitive rather than deterministic.
Longer sequences create more scheduling opportunities for the unsafe placement,
and larger expert-parallel groups add ranks and communication dependencies, so
the probability of exposing the cycle can increase with sequence length and
device count.

## Expected contract

Simpler should define how tasks that can block after occupying an AICore obtain
forward progress. For example:

1. An ordinary task is assumed to run to completion without depending on an
   unscheduled task.
2. A blocking task must declare the producer dependencies that make it safe to
   admit, or be represented as a distinct task type with an explicit progress
   policy.
3. An unmet wait should not consume a core unless the scheduler guarantees that
   every task needed to release it can still run.
4. When the contract is violated, the runtime should fail early or report the
   waiter, awaited event, producer, and core-slot dependency instead of only
   timing out on device.

If intentionally resident communication waiters need to be supported, they may
require a dedicated admission policy such as resource reservation, bounded
co-residency, or group scheduling. Otherwise, producer-to-waiter ordering should
be expressed explicitly in the task graph before the waiter becomes runnable.

## Suggested scope

The current workload should keep the explicit dependency fix in pypto-lib.
Independently, Simpler could improve the scheduler/API in the following areas:

- document the run-to-completion assumption for ordinary tasks;
- identify or annotate tasks containing blocking waits;
- validate that a blocking task has a supported progress path before admission;
- provide actionable diagnostics for resource-wait cycles;
- define a resource guarantee if early resident waiters are an intended feature.

The scheduler does not need to infer MoE-specific producer/consumer relationships.
It does need a clear and enforceable contract for any task that can retain an
execution slot while waiting for work that may not yet have been scheduled.

title: [Performance] Investigate why A5 Scheduler payload/assignment cold-start costs exceed A2/A3 by over 2x
body:
### Platform

a5 (Ascend 950 hardware)

### Runtime Variant

tensormap_and_ringbuffer

### Summary

`SchedulerContext::assign_own_clusters()` has substantially higher cold-start cost on A5 than on A2/A3.

| Stage | A2/A3 mean | A5 mean | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Per-Scheduler payload initialization | ~104 us | ~271 us | **A5 is ~2.6x A2/A3** |
| Full per-Scheduler `assign_own_clusters()` | 115.210 us | 318.755 us | **A5 is ~2.77x A2/A3** |

Each A2/A3 Scheduler initializes 48 double-buffered payloads, while each A5 Scheduler initializes only 42. The A5 slowdown therefore cannot be explained by a larger per-Scheduler payload count. The reason A5 takes more than twice as long needs further investigation.

### Git Commit ID

`9434eb10a7aaa620d1f6cc5e7b534b637f1a96f0`

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Reproduction

Measure payload initialization on A2/A3 and A5 using the same timing boundaries in the current code.

- A2/A3: `src/a2a3/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp`
  - Start point: immediately before the outer payload loop at line 944.
  - End point: immediately after the outer payload loop ends at line 964 and before the function ends at line 965.
- A5: `src/a5/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp`
  - Start point: immediately before the outer payload loop at line 941.
  - End point: immediately after the outer payload loop ends at line 961 and before the function ends at line 962.

The line numbers above refer to commit `9434eb10a7aaa620d1f6cc5e7b534b637f1a96f0`.

A2/A3 instrumentation position:

```cpp
    // Per-dispatch AsyncCtx constant prefill + one-time slab clear for owned cores
    // (mirrors post_handshake_init's all-core loop, restricted to this thread's).
    const uint64_t payload_start = get_sys_cnt_aicpu();  // PAYLOAD TIMING START
    for (int32_t c = 0; c < tracker.get_cluster_count(); c++) {
        // Existing payload initialization loop.
    }
    const uint64_t payload_end = get_sys_cnt_aicpu();  // PAYLOAD TIMING END
}
```

A5 instrumentation position:

```cpp
    // Per-dispatch AsyncCtx constant prefill + one-time slab clear for owned cores
    // (mirrors post_handshake_init's all-core loop, restricted to this thread's).
    const uint64_t payload_start = get_sys_cnt_aicpu();  // PAYLOAD TIMING START
    for (int32_t c = 0; c < tracker.get_cluster_count(); c++) {
        // Existing payload initialization loop.
    }
    const uint64_t payload_end = get_sys_cnt_aicpu();  // PAYLOAD TIMING END
}
```

The boundaries are equivalent on both platforms: the start point is after `CoreTracker` and AIV `sub_block_id` initialization, and the end point is after the complete three-level payload loop. The measured interval therefore excludes `CoreTracker` and AIV `sub_block_id` initialization.

For low-perturbation measurement:

1. Read the AICPU raw system counter once at each boundary.
2. Do not add counter reads or logs inside the payload loop.
3. Print diagnostic results only after the cold path has completed.
4. Use independent Python cold starts and keep the workload, DFX settings, and collection configuration consistent across platforms.
5. Report both the per-Scheduler mean and the slowest Scheduler in each run; do not sum parallel Scheduler times and interpret the result as wall-clock latency.

The timed interval includes initialization of:

- `AsyncCtx` completion pointers and capacity;
- deferred-completion slab `count` and `error_code`;
- DMA workspace pointers;
- local/global context argument addresses.

### Expected Performance

The A5 payload initialization path should not retain an unexplained greater-than-2x cold-start gap relative to A2/A3 despite initializing fewer payloads per Scheduler. A same-configuration baseline should identify which A5-specific memory, layout, or runtime behavior accounts for the additional time and determine whether it is avoidable.

### Actual Performance

Current measurements show:

- A2/A3 payload initialization mean: 104.221 us;
- A5 payload initialization mean: 270.553 us, approximately 2.6x A2/A3;
- A2/A3 full assignment mean: 115.210 us;
- A5 topo-on full assignment mean: 318.755 us, approximately 2.77x A2/A3.

The existing full-assignment measurements were collected with different chip-swimlane configurations, so the 2.77x figure establishes the scale of the difference rather than a strict controlled architectural comparison. The payload measurements use the code boundaries documented above and are the primary signal to investigate.

### Profiling Data (Optional)

The payload loop touches both buffers for every core owned by a Scheduler. It initializes fixed payload fields and resets only the deferred-completion slab header (`count` and `error_code`); it does not clear the 64 completion entries.

Observed cold-versus-hot behavior suggests that sparse first-touch cost is a likely contributor, but the underlying mechanism has not been established. Investigation should distinguish among page/TLB/cache residency, concurrent cold writes by multiple Scheduler threads, and A5/A2A3 layout or alignment differences.

### Additional Context

This is a startup performance investigation, not an affinity-gate regression. Bypassing the gate does not remove `assign_own_clusters()` work; it can only move unrecorded initialization before the chip-swimlane relative time origin.

Related: #545, #984

title: [Bug] host_build_graph: --dump-args selective (L1) and hybrid (L3) produce empty/degraded output
body:
### Platform

a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C hardware)

### Runtime Variant

host_build_graph

### Description

On `host_build_graph` (hbg), `--dump-args` only works at level **2 (FULL)**. Levels **1 (PARTIAL)** and **3 (HYBRID)** silently produce no useful output:

- **PARTIAL (1)** — dumps **nothing**.
- **HYBRID (3)** — dumps all task metadata, but the payload for `Arg::dump()`-marked tensors is **never captured**, which compromises `simpler_setup.tools.core_swimlane`'s `--dump-args 3` replay.

Root cause: the per-task dump selection tables (`set_dump_args_task_mask`, `set_dump_args_task_scalar_dtypes`) are populated **only** from the orchestrator. In hbg the orchestrator runs on the **host**, so these calls resolve to the weak **no-op stubs** in `host_orch_compat_stubs.cpp`, leaving the device-side mask table empty. The device scheduler's `should_dump_task()` then returns false for every task in selective mode. FULL works only because selective mode is off (mask is not consulted). Note: even FULL loses scalar dtypes (they fall back to `UINT64`) for the same reason.

This is the host-orch weak-stub class of hbg DFX gaps tracked under #1706.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
1. Run an hbg scene test with selective dump:
   pytest tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/dump_args --platform a2a3 -d <dev> --dump-args 1
2. Inspect <output_prefix>/args_dump/ — it is empty (no per-task args).
3. Repeat with --dump-args 3 and feed the result to
   `python -m simpler_setup.tools.core_swimlane ...` — the Arg::dump()-marked
   tensor payloads are missing.
4. --dump-args 2 (FULL) works, confirming the capture path itself is fine.
```

### Expected Behavior

`--dump-args 1` dumps exactly the `Arg::dump()`-marked args; `--dump-args 3` dumps all metadata plus payload for `Arg::dump()`-marked tensors — matching `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` behavior.

### Actual Behavior

`--dump-args 1` dumps nothing; `--dump-args 3` drops the marked-tensor payloads. Scalar dtypes fall back to `UINT64` at all levels.

Key locations:
- Host no-op stubs: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/host/host_orch_compat_stubs.cpp:31-36`
- Orchestrator (host) call sites: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:1284-1296`
- Working device capture (needs the mask): `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_dispatch.cpp:242`, `scheduler_completion.cpp:176`

Suggested fix: carry `dump_arg_mask` / scalar dtypes in the H2D task image (the host orchestrator knows them at build time) and have the device scheduler read them from the image instead of the runtime table.

### Git Commit ID

50c0660646217f1b56172a81990279bd066ed971

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1706. Sibling hbg DFX gaps filed separately (scope-stats inert; chip-swimlane L4 no-op).

title: [Bug] host_build_graph: --enable-scope-stats produces empty scope_stats.jsonl (inert on hbg)
body:
### Platform

a2a3 (Ascend 910B/C hardware)

### Runtime Variant

host_build_graph

### Description

On `host_build_graph` (hbg), `--enable-scope-stats` produces an empty (no-scope) `scope_stats.jsonl`. The capability is effectively **inert** on hbg.

Root cause: scope-stats is an orchestrator-driven measurement (per-scope ring/heap/tensormap occupancy at `begin_scope`/`end_scope`). In hbg the orchestrator runs on the **host**, where:
- `scope_stats_begin` / `scope_stats_end` / `scope_stats_on_fatal` / `scope_stats_set_pending_site` resolve to the weak **no-op stubs** in `host_orch_compat_stubs.cpp`, and the enable gate `is_scope_stats_enabled()` is a weak-false stub, so the orchestrator records nothing.
- There is **no device-side (scheduler) driver** for scope-stats in hbg — the on-device driver (`scope_stats_set_ring_capacity` / `set_tensormap_capacity` / `aicpu_flush_buffers`) is called only from the `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` AICPU executor; hbg's `aicpu_executor.cpp` includes the header but makes none of those calls.

The host `device_runner` still flips the DFX bit and drains device shared memory when the flag is passed, but the arena stays empty → empty JSONL. There is no hbg scope_stats scene test (only tmr has one), consistent with this being unimplemented for hbg. Documented as tmr-only in #995.

This is the host-orch weak-stub class of hbg DFX gaps tracked under #1706.

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
1. Run any hbg example with scope-stats enabled:
   pytest tests/st/a2a3/host_build_graph/paged_attention --platform a2a3 -d <dev> --enable-scope-stats
2. Inspect <output_prefix>/scope_stats.jsonl — it is empty / contains no scope records.
3. Contrast with tensormap_and_ringbuffer, where the same flag yields populated per-scope peaks.
```

### Expected Behavior

`--enable-scope-stats` on hbg emits per-scope ring/heap/tensormap occupancy peaks to `scope_stats.jsonl` (consumable by `simpler_setup.tools.scope_stats_plot`), matching `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`.

### Actual Behavior

`scope_stats.jsonl` is empty; nothing is ever recorded (host recorder is a no-op stub; device has no scheduler-side driver).

Key locations:
- Host no-op stubs: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/host/host_orch_compat_stubs.cpp:39-46`
- Orchestrator (host) call sites: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:939-945,971-977`
- Device driver present only in tmr: `src/a2a3/runtime/tensormap_and_ringbuffer/aicpu/aicpu_executor.cpp:652,657,697,719`

Suggested fix: since scopes are fully known at host graph-build time for hbg, implement a **host-side** scope-stats collector (replace the no-op stubs with a real host recorder feeding the existing `scope_stats.jsonl` exporter).

### Git Commit ID

50c0660646217f1b56172a81990279bd066ed971

### Host Platform

Linux (aarch64)

### Additional Context

Related: #1706, #995. Sibling hbg DFX gaps filed separately (arg-dump selective/hybrid empty; chip-swimlane L4 no-op).

title: [Code Health] host_build_graph: chip-swimlane level 4 (orch phases) is a no-op; device allocates+flushes a dead orch-phase pool
body:
### Category

Dead Code / Unused Dependencies

### Component

Orchestration

### Description

On `host_build_graph` (hbg), `--enable-chip-swimlane 4` (orchestrator phases) collects **no orchestrator records** — it behaves identically to level 3 plus an empty `aicpu_orchestrator_phases[]` array. Two problems:

1. **Misleading level.** Level 4 is advertised (`--enable-chip-swimlane` help, `profiling_levels.md`) but yields nothing on hbg, because the orchestrator runs on the **host**, where `chip_swimlane_aicpu_record_orch_phase` is a weak **no-op** (the strong symbol lives only in the AICPU `.so`, which never orchestrates in hbg).
2. **Dead code on the device.** The scheduler cold path still initializes an orch-phase pool (`orch_phase_threads = 1`) and flushes it in `on_orchestration_done`, even though it is always empty in hbg.

Levels 1–3 (AICore timing / AICPU dispatch-finish / scheduler phases) work correctly on hbg — this is only about level 4. The `swimlane_converter.py` already tolerates an empty orch array (no orch lane is emitted), so there is no crash, just dead work and a level that promises data it never delivers.

This is the host-orch class of hbg DFX gaps tracked under #1706; the host-side orchestrator-phase collection overlaps with the host swimlane L3/L4 request in #1708.

### Location

```markdown
- Weak no-op record fn (host build): `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/orchestrator_core/pto_orchestrator.cpp:134,146`
- Dead orch-phase pool init: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp:840`
- Dead orch-phase pool flush: `src/a2a3/runtime/host_build_graph/runtime/scheduler/scheduler_cold_path.cpp:1060`
```

### Proposed Fix

Two options (pick per the direction chosen for #1708):

- **Honest-minimal:** cap hbg at level 3 (reject/clamp level 4 for hbg with a clear message) and delete the device-side empty orch-phase pool init + flush. Smallest, removes the dead code and the misleading level.
- **Feature-complete:** implement **host-side** orchestrator-phase collection (the host orchestrator's per-task submit timing) feeding the existing `chip_swimlane_records.json` orch lane, so level 4 delivers real host-orch timing. Larger; aligns with #1708.

### Priority

Medium (minor risk, should fix in next few releases)

title: [Feature] host_build_graph: emit Resolve / AsyncPoll / Dummy sched-phase bars in L3 chip swimlane
body:
### Summary

At chip-swimlane level 3 (SCHED_PHASES), `host_build_graph` (hbg) emits only a subset of the scheduler phase bars that `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` (tmr) emits. hbg emits **Complete / Dispatch / EarlyDispatch / Drain / DrainPrepare / DrainPublish**; it does **not** emit **Resolve**, **AsyncPoll**, or **Dummy**, even though all three mechanisms exist in hbg's scheduler. This is an observability gap: real scheduler work is invisible in the swimlane (folded into other bars or unlabeled).

(Note: **Release** is intentionally out of scope — hbg is whole-graph-resident and does not reclaim ring slots at runtime, so a Release bar would be meaningless for hbg. Only Resolve / AsyncPoll / Dummy are missing capabilities.)

### Motivation / Use Case

The L3 sched-phase swimlane is the primary tool for attributing AICPU scheduler time. On hbg today:
- **Dependency resolution** (fanout/consumer walk) is real work but is folded into the **Complete** bar, so you cannot see how much time resolution costs vs. pure completion detection — exactly the quantity the hbg 3S+1P scheduler proposal needs to measure.
- **Async completion polling** (URMA / aicore_mailbox deferred completion) runs every scheduler loop but is unattributed — the header even notes it explicitly (`async-wait drain path has no Resolve swimlane bar attached`).
- **Dummy-task retirement** happens inline via `dummy_ready_queue` but is invisible.

Without these bars, hbg swimlane time attribution is incomplete and cannot be compared like-for-like against tmr where these phases are already broken out.

### Proposed API / Behavior

Emit the three additional `SchedPhaseKind` records from hbg's scheduler at the sites where the work already happens, mirroring how tmr labels them — but reflecting hbg's own structure (e.g. Resolve is the inner fanout-walk portion of Complete, not a standalone pass):

- **Resolve** — around the `on_task_complete` consumer/fanout walk (`scheduler_completion.cpp` / `scheduler_dispatch.cpp:903-964`, `resolved_this_pass`), so Resolve time is split out of the Complete bar.
- **AsyncPoll** — around `AsyncWaitList::poll_and_complete` (`pto_scheduler.h:1153`), attributing the async-drain path.
- **Dummy** — around the `dummy_ready_queue` inline-retire path (`pto_scheduler.h:467,488`).

The swimlane framework already defines these enumerators (`chip_swimlane_profiling.h`) and `swimlane_converter.py` already renders them for tmr, so no post-process changes are expected — this is device-side emission only.

### Alternatives Considered

- Leave folded into Complete — rejected: hides the resolve/async/dummy split that hbg scheduler tuning (e.g. the 3S+1P dedicated-resolution-thread proposal) depends on measuring.
- Mirror tmr's phase structure verbatim — rejected: hbg and tmr are different schedulers; the bars must reflect hbg's model (Resolve as an inner slice of Complete, no Release).

### Additional Context

Parent tracking: #995. Sibling hbg DFX gaps: #1800, #1801, #1802 — but this one is **independent of those** (they fix host-orch weak stubs; this is on-device scheduler instrumentation). Distinct from #1708 (host-side orchestrator swimlane). All three mechanisms confirmed present in a2a3 hbg at commit 50c0660.

title: [Performance] host_build_graph: activate graph nodes incrementally as they materialize
body:
# Human Summary

In HBG the task graph is sent to the device and fully expanded before computation starts. This PR pipelines the expansion and the computation so that AI cores can start doing useful work as soon as the first task is processed. This saves a bunch of initialization time.

# AI Summary

The on-device Graph scheduler expanded a `GRAPH` task into **all** its nodes before dispatching **any** of them — `graph_execution_materialize_slice` reached `PREPARED` only after the last node, and `activate_prepared_graph` routed the roots only at that point. For a large graph the AICores idle through the entire expansion. On the qwen3-14B 3-layer decode this front-loaded ramp is **~530 µs per layer** with every core waiting.

This routes roots (and any node whose producers have all completed) **as soon as they materialize**, once the outer `GRAPH` task's external-dependency gate has opened, so compute overlaps the remaining expansion.

## How it's made safe — and what makes it possible

Dispatching a node before the whole graph is materialized means a producer can complete while a later consumer is still being registered — the exact hazard the `PREPARED` gate existed to prevent. This change is only possible because of the **polling-completion scheduler**: the per-slot `completion_flags` byte + `task_state` completion mirror introduced for `tensormap_and_ringbuffer` in **#1137** and adapted to `host_build_graph` in **#1435**. That model lets a consumer answer "has this producer finished?" by reading a flag, so a producer completing mid-expansion is *discovered*, not missed. Under the older pure wake-list model this would have been unsafe — which is precisely why the whole-graph `PREPARED` gate existed. Three things close the hazard:

- **Flag-safe registration.** Materialization-time registration moves from `register_initial_graph_waiter` (a raw wake-list store that assumed no producer could complete during expansion) to `register_graph_wake`, which resolves a producer that completed mid-expansion through its `task_state` completion flag (the #1137/#1435 mechanism) instead of losing the wake. This machinery already existed on the live wake path; this change simply routes materialization through it.
- **Topological order.** The definition is validated to be topologically ordered (every producer index < consumer index), so every producer a materialized node references is already constructed. `execution.nodes` is published at `MATERIALIZING` (under `materialize_busy`) so the wake path can read producer slots during expansion.
- **Idempotent root routing.** Roots reach the ready queue through `route_cursor`, a monotonic per-execution cursor that makes routing idempotent across the per-slice calls and the final call at the activation meet — each root is pushed exactly once. Non-roots reach the queue only through their producers' wake list, unchanged.

## Testing

- **Correctness:** the three `graph_execution` scene tests (2D replay, AIC+AIV, MIX-SPMD) and the **qwen3-14B 3-layer graph-execution golden** pass, including a 3-round replay. A 45-run repeat of the three graph-exec tests passes 45/45 (initial rapid-repeat failures were host-side `halMemCtl` MMIO contention from process churn — a different binary, before the scheduler runs — and vanish once process starts are spaced).
- **Performance** (qwen3-14B 3-layer, a2a3 onboard, same-device A/B, 15 rounds):

  | | Avg device_wall |
  |---|--:|
  | baseline | 3397.8 µs |
  | incremental | 3247.1 µs |
  | **delta** | **−150.7 µs (−4.4%)** |

  The chip swimlane confirms compute begins overlapping graph expansion (cores busy at ~400 µs) instead of waiting for it (~600 µs baseline). The first-compute start is still bounded by the outer task's external-dependency latency, so the recovered time is the expansion **tail**, not an earlier start.

## Scope

- a2a3 + a5 `host_build_graph`, same commit (identical graph scheduler). a5 is **compile-verified only** — the dev box is a2a3 silicon.
- Only affects the graph-execution path; non-graph dispatch is untouched.

title: CI: reduce packaging, profiling, and unit-test overhead
body:
## Summary

- Reuse process-global runtime helpers and limit no-hardware UT builds to the simulator platforms they exercise.
- Generate per-target profiling headers so all six flag combinations and both simulator architectures reuse unaffected objects.
- Use an empty job-local ccache across packaging modes, normalize the macOS deployment target across all five modes, and fall back when ccache is unavailable.
- Keep sanitizer builds on one host ABI and isolate sanitizer state between tests.
- Build A3 C++ UT before NPU allocation, then run Python and C++ hardware UT under one allocation.
- Validate packaging installs outside the source tree and keep every mode fully clean.
- Upload POD diagnostics best-effort so artifact failures cannot replace the test result.

## Scope and safety

- Keeps profiling in one job; no job splitting and no coverage reduction.
- Keeps one real cold build per packaging job and does not restore compiler objects across jobs.
- ccache only reuses objects when compiler inputs match; CMake configuration, linking, installation, and smoke checks still run for every mode.
- The macOS target is the runner's existing major.minor target, made explicit so pip and direct CMake receive the same compiler input.
- Self-hosted runners without ccache keep the original uncached behavior.
- Does not change the unrelated worker admission-fence timing test.

## Observed CI result

Run 31666256787, before the macOS target-normalization experiment:

- Profiling: 11m19s baseline to 6m33s total; the 12 build/test groups fell from about 9m30s to 4m51s.
- Packaging Ubuntu: 10m34s to 4m00s total, with 79.14% ccache hits.
- Packaging macOS: 10m19s to 9m50s total, with 62.72% hits.
- All profiling, packaging, simulator, hardware, and POD jobs passed.
- macOS Python UT hit an existing timing-boundary flake: 0.999468792s measured against a 1.0s assertion. This PR intentionally does not modify that unrelated test.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current upstream/main and kept as one commit.
- Targeted runtime/toolchain UT: 66 passed.
- Profiling matrix: 6 configurations × 2 simulator architectures passed.
- Packaging matrix passed on Ubuntu and macOS before target normalization.
- YAML and pre-commit checks passed for the normalization change.
- Fresh CI is measuring macOS packaging time and ccache hits for the normalized target.

title: tensormap_and_ringbuffer: split fanin edges into orthogonal WAIT/RETAIN flags (#1375)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1375 (PR1 of 2 — the WAIT/RETAIN infrastructure).

In `tensormap_and_ringbuffer`, one fanin edge coupled two semantics: **WAIT**
(the consumer waits for the producer) and **RETAIN** (the producer's slot +
packed output stay alive until the consumer releases them). Coupling them
retains modifier producers for the consumer's whole lifetime even though only
ordering is needed, and blocks the transitive-reduction work that must drop a
redundant ordering edge while keeping a required lifetime reference.

This PR makes the two semantics orthogonal per edge and splits the accounting.
It lands identically in **a2a3 and a5**.

## What changed

- **`DepFlags { DEP_WAIT, DEP_RETAIN }`** in `pto_types.h`.
- **Storage**: pack the 2 flag bits into the low bits of the producer slot
  pointer, for both the inline fanin array and the spill pool
  (`PTO2TaskSlotState` is `alignas(64)`). `sizeof` unchanged; no new payload
  field — which also removes the separate-mask/`init()`-order hazard the
  reference prototype had.
- **Construction**: creator (`owner_task_id`) → `WAIT|RETAIN`; tensormap
  modifier → `WAIT`; explicit deps default `WAIT|RETAIN`, with a new
  `CoreTaskArgsWithDeps::add_dep_wait()` for ordering-only deps. Duplicate
  producers **OR-accumulate** their flags on dedup (no first-wins ordering).
- **Accounting**: readiness (`fanin_count`, `fanout_head` linkage, dep_pool
  reservation) counts `DEP_WAIT` edges only. A `WAIT`-without-`RETAIN` edge
  releases its submit→wire pin **at wiring** (and on the all-completed fast
  path), so a modifier producer can be CONSUMED without waiting for this
  consumer. `on_task_release` releases `DEP_RETAIN` edges only.
- **DFX**: dep_gen replay threads `DepFlags` through the oracle, records
  `"flags"` per edge in `deps.json`, and the differential gate now compares the
  `(producer → flags)` mapping instead of the producer-id set alone.

No `RETAIN`-only edge is produced yet — nothing generates one until the
transitive-reduction pass, which is the **follow-up PR2** (device-side 1-hop,
per the discussion on #1375). This PR is the enabling representation +
accounting it builds on, plus the modifier early-consume win.

## Tests

- **cpput** (a2a3 + a5, 97/97): fanin-pool `DepFlags` round-trip across inline
  **and** spill; wiring regressions (ordering-only producer released at wiring
  vs. retention held until `on_task_release`, including a spilled `RETAIN`
  edge); orchestrator-level tests for a WAIT-only explicit dep, OR-fold of two
  discovery kinds on one producer (inline **and** spill region, asserting the
  spilled edge's folded flags), and the all-completed fast-path pin release.
- **sim scene tests**: `dfx/dep_gen` on a2a3sim + a5sim (exercises the
  flag-aware replay gate and `deps.json` flags end-to-end); `dummy_task` and
  `mixed_example` on both sims.
- **onboard (a2a3, real silicon via task-submit)**: full
  `tests/st/a2a3/tensormap_and_ringbuffer` scene-test suite — **33 passed**; a
  **30-iteration stress loop** over the dependency-heavy `mixed_example` +
  `alternating_matmul_add` (exercising the modifier WAIT-only early-release path
  and slot reuse) — **all passed**, no `507018` / hang / wrong result. This is
  the concurrency validation for the one real behavior change (early pin release
  makes `COMPLETED → CONSUMED → reset_for_reuse` a common path).

## Notes for review

- The a2a3 and a5 diffs are symmetric (identical per-file line counts).
- `host_build_graph` has its own `append_fanin_or_fail` and is otherwise
  untouched; the only hbg change is one comment line, fixing a now-dangling
  `fanin_inline_slot_states` reference to hbg's actual `fanin_local_ids` after
  the payload field rename.
- **One open point for the team:** `or_flags_into_existing` uses `always_assert`
  when a deduped producer is somehow absent from the builder (a seen-set/builder
  desync — currently unreachable). This is a loud device failure rather than a
  silent weak-semantics degrade; flagging the "crash-not-continue" choice for
  confirmation. Can switch to `report_fatal` if preferred.

title: Fix A2A3 repeated-run AICore stream regression
body:
## Summary

- retain proven-complete per-slot A2A3 AICore streams while no new AICore code has been published
- mark every retained slot stream stale only after a successful AICore H2D upload; content-hash dedup hits do not invalidate streams
- recreate stale streams on the next acquire, while preserving conservative destruction for unproven runs and failed-destroy retry ownership
- cover repeated reuse, deduplicated registration, concurrently resident callables, cross-slot `A -> B -> A` address-recycle publication, retirement gating, and exact stream-creation counts
- update `docs/task-flow.md` with the actual content-hash allocation and publication invariant

Fixes #1791

## Validation

- changed-file pre-commit: all hooks passed (`clang-format`, `clang-tidy`, `cpplint`, `ruff`, `pyright`, `markdownlint`)
- `RunStreamSlots` C++ unit tests: 19/19 passed with GCC 15 on LCW
- A2A3 architecture probe: passed on `task-submit` (`task_20260814_024716_37579914368`)
- GitHub CI on `a9ec96bb2`: 18/18 checks completed with no failures (17 success, expected `deploy` skip), including `ut-a2a3`, `ut-a5`, `st-onboard-a2a3`, `st-onboard-a5`, `st-pod-onboard-a2a3`, both A2A3/A5 simulation matrices, packaging, profiling, and pre-commit

An additional LCW mixed-venv targeted run (`task_20260814_025329_67147427068`) reached its 600-second pytest session timeout in `native_run_lifecycle::test_run` before any assertion result. It is not treated as product evidence; the clean GitHub `st-onboard-a2a3` run above passed the full suite on this exact head.

The stream-creation assertions validate the mechanism. The issue-specific HCA/SWA latency benchmark pins older PyPTO/PTO-ISA revisions, so no mixed-revision latency number is reported as comparable performance evidence.

title: Fix: preserve args dump selection in host-built graphs
body:
Host-built graph orchestration runs outside AICPU, so its dump-mask and scalar-dtype table updates resolved to host-side no-op stubs. Partial dumps consequently selected no tasks, while hybrid dumps emitted metadata without marked tensor payloads.

Embed the selection mask, ambiguity flags, and scalar dtypes in each HBG task payload and cached Graph definition. Consume that metadata in dispatch, completion, and timeout dump paths while retaining the existing AICPU side table for tensormap-and-ringbuffer.

Cover direct submission and Graph replay on both architectures, and exercise partial and hybrid manifests on a2a3 onboard plus a2a3sim/a5sim.

Fixes #1800

title: [Bug] Worker.close() still leaves child processes after sticky shutdown fix on a2a3
body:
### Diagnosis

Simpler child teardown/reap — `Worker.close()` still leaves child processes beyond the 10-second close budget even though the installed version contains the sticky `_OFF_SHUTDOWN` fix from #1663.

This is therefore not the original SHUTDOWN-clobber mechanism tracked in #1562.

### Description

The issue reproduced twice during successful eight-card DeepSeek V4 MTP generation on a2a3.

In both cases:

- The HTTP/offline request completed successfully.
- Exactly 20 output tokens were generated.
- MTP completion and profiling finished.
- Shutdown then reported exactly two surviving Simpler child processes.
- Python's `resource_tracker` subsequently reported two leaked shared-memory objects.

Observed runs:

| Task | Devices | Surviving children |
|---|---|---|
| `task_20260812_011011_19195415170` | `1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15` | `2640883, 2655062` |
| `task_20260812_021620_79277523625` | `0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14` | `1043175, 1046035` |

The second run used host STRACE with device STRACE disabled. Its request completed in 2.63 seconds with 20 tokens and MTP acceptance 10/11 before teardown failed.

### Command or Request

```bash
task-submit \
  --device 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14 \
  --max-time 0 \
  --timeout 0 \
  --env PTOAS_ROOT=/data/yangyaodong/.cache/codex/ptoas-0.57-cp310 \
  --env PTO2_RING_HEAP=3221225472 \
  --run "bash .agents/skills/profile-dsv4-serving-strace/scripts/run_profile.sh \
    --model-dir /data/models/dsv4-flash-w8a8 \
    --use-compile-cache \
    --devices 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14 \
    --artifact-dir artifacts/dsv4-async-profile-even-final-20260812 \
    --run-id async-profile-even-final-20260812"
```

Relevant runtime configuration:

```text
PYPTO_RUNTIME_LOG=v9
SIMPLER_DEVICE_STRACE_ENABLE=0
PTO2_RING_HEAP=3221225472
PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=131072
PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=131072
SIMPLER_OP_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT_US=400000000
SIMPLER_STREAM_SYNC_TIMEOUT_MS=440000
SIMPLER_SCHEDULER_TIMEOUT_MS=320000
SERVING_WORKER_STEP_TIMEOUT=1800
```

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| pypto-serving | `1a16e2c` plus local async submit/reclaim changes |
| pypto-lib | `384553ad` |
| pypto | `ed2aaa18` |
| simpler | package `0.1.0`; installed source contains sticky `_OFF_SHUTDOWN` |
| ptoas | `0.57` |
| CANN | `9.0.0` |
| torch / torch-npu | `2.10.0` / `2.10.0` |

### Host Platform

Linux aarch64

### Device / Platform

Eight a2a3 NPUs. Reproduced independently on the all-odd and all-even device groups.

### Model

DeepSeek V4 MTP, checkpoint `/data/models/dsv4-flash-w8a8`.

### Expected Behavior

After a completed request, `Worker.close()` should terminate and reap every chip child within the close path without reporting leaked shared memory.

### Actual Behavior

```text
INFO pypto_serving.serving.engine.async_engine: Engine loop stopped
02:23:13.956 INFO | Worker exiting
02:23:26.224 ERROR | Failed to close PyPTO runner for model dsv4-flash-w8a8
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../simpler/worker.py", line 9240, in <lambda>
    _step(lambda: self._reap_child_groups(groups, reap_deadline))
  File ".../simpler/worker.py", line 9163, in _reap_child_groups
    raise errors[0]
TimeoutError: child process(es) [1043175, 1046035] did not exit within the close budget

resource_tracker.py:224: UserWarning:
resource_tracker: There appear to be 2 leaked shared_memory objects to clean up at shutdown
```

The earlier run produced the same signature:

```text
TimeoutError: child process(es) [2640883, 2655062] did not exit within the close budget
resource_tracker: There appear to be 2 leaked shared_memory objects to clean up at shutdown
```

### Additional Context

Related issue: #1562.

That issue was closed after #1663 introduced a one-way sticky shutdown word, preventing an in-flight control transition from overwriting SHUTDOWN. The currently installed source contains `_OFF_SHUTDOWN` and `_SHUTDOWN_REQUESTED`, so this recurrence should rule out that original clobber race.

The remaining likely categories are:

1. child device/CANN teardown occasionally exceeds the fixed 10-second budget;
2. a child is genuinely wedged after receiving sticky shutdown;
3. a different close/register or teardown ordering race remains.

It would be useful for `_reap_child_groups` to include each survivor's sticky shutdown state and, if practical, its current teardown phase in the timeout diagnostics.

title: Fix: preserve A2A3 early dispatch on queue overflow
body:
## Summary

- increase the A2A3 per-shape early-dispatch candidate queue from 64 to 256;
- roll an early-dispatch candidate from `STAGING` back to `NONE` when its
  initial queue publication fails, preserving the ordinary readiness path;
- add a wiring test for the queue-overflow fallback.

## Root cause

One wide producer may publish substantially more early-dispatch candidates
than there are physical cores. DeepSeek V4 EP8 routed experts expose the
boundary clearly: balanced 64-token routing creates 64 local gate/up MM
candidates and passes, while 96 or 128 tokens create a burst of 128 candidates
and can stall with the former 64-entry queue.

The scheduler also ignored `push_tagged()` failure after changing a candidate
from `NONE` to `STAGING`. An unqueued candidate could therefore remain in a
speculative state without an early-dispatch drain owning it. The rollback uses
a compare-exchange so a concurrent producer release continues to own any state
transition it has already made.

The larger queue absorbs the known wide-producer burst. The fallback keeps
overflow semantically safe rather than relying on capacity alone.

## Validation

- A2A3 `test_wiring`: all 37 tests pass, including the new
  `EarlyDispatchQueueOverflowFallsBackToNormalDispatch` case.
- DeepSeek V4 EP8 MoE, 4 consecutive epochs, 128 tokens, all baseline
  `allow_early_resolve` hints: PASS.
- DeepSeek V4 CP8/EP8/TP4 synthetic prefill forward:
  - 6 layers, 1 GiB ring heap: PASS;
  - 43 layers, 1 GiB ring heap: PASS with all persistent outputs accepted,
    finite/nonzero hidden states, and valid logits from both TP4 groups.

A diagnostic build retaining queue capacity 64 but adding the rollback made
the 96-token workload pass, while 128 tokens still stalled. This confirms that
the state fallback and sufficient publication-burst capacity are both needed.

title: SPMD paged attention fails with multi-block and multi-core A5 workloads

## Current status

The A5 SPMD paged-attention port can complete a small zero-query flow, but larger workloads and non-uniform attention are not yet reliable.

### A5 results

- batch=1, context_len=128, zero query: passes golden
- batch=2, context_len=128, zero query: passes golden
- batch=24, context_len=128: completes, max golden diff about 0.1137
